I am a licensed Loan Officer and recently ran into an audit finding with UWM on a previous client. This part is information prior to my loan which I believe can be beneficial to the entire complaint. The audit team asked for documents and proof of the properties being rented to offset his XXXX so the outcome of his approval wouldn't change. About a week later they notified us that he has been black listed for undisclosed properties after the property had been sold and the loan paid in full. I relayed the information to him with their decision. It turns out that the other properties were with UWM as well through a different Loan officer in another state. UWM ( United Wholesale Mortgage ) systems for checks and balances should have triggered or caught this in my opinion. If all of his info is on each property how did UWM not catch thi s prior to them closing back to back? This shows severe issues in the UWM system process which puts the consumer at risk. Not to mention it puts UWM at risk as well. This is when things really started showing up at my door step. A few months later I needed to refinance my own property. I started to notice or feel that I was being targeted and wondered if I myself had been flagged due to the previous incident. In a nutshell I was pushed over to having a higher rate and payment do to negligence of the UWM team. We clearly know this is illegal and is a ploy for UWM to make more money with me being at a higher rate. At closing I signed the anti steering document as there was no steering by XXXX Mortgage, I feel confident that there was steering by the underwriters to push me into products that would have been more beneficial for the company. I will explain this further below as I explain the series of events. On another occasion the underwriter requested a CPA letter. I gladly reached out and copied the exact request from underwriting that I received from the processor and sent it over to my CPA. United Wholesale Mortgage is currently processing a loan application for a mutual client and we were provided a CPA explanation letter on your letterhead and bearing your signature. Your assistance is appreciated. Please feel free to reach out directly with any questions or concerns. It appears this was perfectly set up to try and entrap me and again to deny the loan. The font in the letter is slightly different. However, there is a repeated trend in how my account is being handled by UWM. This appears to be Overt Evidence and a violation of fair lending. Let 's move on to credit accounts with installments less than 10 months. UWM refused to make changes though statements proved that there were less than 10 months. As defined under Real Estate Settlement Procedures Act ( RESPA ) Fair Debt Collection Practices Act as well as the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ), it is required that all accounting be applied based on actual amounts that are due. I have been paying an extra {$600.00} to {$700.00} per month towards negative escrow, which has not been applied accordingly. The monthly statements issued by SLS show that the minimum monthly payments due are {$1600.00}. The principal payment is {$200.00}, with interest being {$360.00} per month, which leaves the balance {$1000.00} to be applied to escrow ( ex B ). The {$1000.00} has not been applied towards escrow due, instead it has been held in suspense accounts and re-allocated. Per CFPB rule 1026.41, the amount due, has shown more prominently than other disclosures on the page and, if the transaction has multiple payment options, the amount due falls under each of the payment options and CFPB rule. Furthermore, the rule states that the monthly payment amount, including a breakdown showing how much, if any, will be applied to principal, interest, and escrow and, if a mortgage loan has multiple payment options, a breakdown of each of the payment options along with information on whether the principal balance will increase, decrease, or stay the same for each option listed must be shown. Since there is a lack of transparency in the negative escrow accounting, we are requesting that all payments be reallocated and applied to the negative escrow amount currently listed as {$21000.00}. CFPB Rule 1024.17 also has standards listed that must be adhered to in relation to escrow. if a servicer advances funds for a borrower, then the servicer must perform an escrow account analysis before seeking repayment of the deficiency. Proper analysis is not being performed to bring the escrow account out of delinquency.

In XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX, I contacted Banner Bank to have my PMI payment removed as I believed I qualified since houses on my block were selling in the high XXXX, which was higher than the fair market value range I needed to get my XXXX removed. Removing the PMI payment was very important to me because I had two XXXX XXXX XXXX and had not been able to work as much as I had previously. Removing the PMI would have been a huge relief for me and I was extremely excited at the prospect of it being eliminated. Unfortunately, the first BPO value was flawed and a second corrective BPO had to be done, at Banner Banks expense, as they ultimately took responsibility, but only after I had to fight to prove to them that it was their fault that I was unable to appeal the first BPO, causing a new one to be required. Still, the corrective BPO which revealed my true home value took nine months to get due to the errors, mismanagement, misconduct, unwillingness to help. The overall incompetence on the part of the two Banner staff members, XXXX XXXX and XXXX XXXX, resuled in me paying thousands in unnecessary PMI and interest on a higher principal during the months it took for Banner to process the corrective BPO. Not to mention the change in market which no doubt had an impact on the new BPO which was ultimately done in XX/XX/XXXX. It is the relief from those unnecessary PMI, and higher interest payments, that I am seeking today since it took almost a year of my life to deal with, and monitor, this situation while these staff members refused, then slowly, attempted to correct their mistakes and get on top of the matter. It isnt my job to do this, but it was theirs. I believe they paid for the corrective BPO in part to cover their legal exposure since I pointed out their errors in writing. While on the phone, XXXX was very clear - and insistent- that it was not their problem, or error to repair, and they would not be taking any steps to make things right. As I expected, the new BPO came back XXXX higher than the first flawed BPO. Because of this difference, I was able to pay down the {$2400.00} difference to get from 75.7 % LTV to 75 % exactly in order to successfully have the PMI removed. In early XX/XX/XXXX, I paid the {$2400.00} to have the XXXX XXXX monthly PMI payment removed from my regular mortgage payment. Despite the pay down amount not being applied to my regular mortgage payment, it was worth it to have all the money going to me rather than the banks insurance company. While any one of these things may have been minor, it is the sum total of these mistakes that has resulted in an unreasonable and unfair loss of money for me, and for which I would like Banner Bank to remedy. However, XXXX, on behalf of Banner Bank, doesnt care to acknowledge how this protracted XXXX month process due to her errors and foot dragging resulted in nine unnecessary PMI payments, and additional interest, while she got her act together to get the 2nd corrective BPO completed. XXXX dismissiveness is the reason I am opening a ticket here. I truly feel someone else needs to step in to make my reasonable request for reimbursement for the nine PMI payment happen, and to monitor these agents in order to prevent future harm to other Banner Bank clients. If it were not for them, I would have had a smooth and succinct BPO process, as is typical. Going back to how this all started. in XXXX XXXX, I was working with XXXX who took my information, agreed I was eligible based on the other requirements to remove my PMI, and set me up for a BPO. At that time, she took the money out of my account to pay for the BPO. I was told I would be contacted in about a week to schedule the appraisal. I waited and waited. Eventually a broker contact me for the BPO but he was rushed, told me the deadline was the next day, and he needed to come by asap to get it done. I accommodated. Weeks passedagain, no information or updatesfinally I contacted XXXX who said that the letter had been sent out a month prior but provided no additional information. I got the letter in the mail a few days later with a date confirming the decision was from a month prior and the PMI removal was denied. Reviewing the BPO it was clear that it was not accurate. The BPO did not use relevant comps and did not include any improvements made to the house. I contacted XXXX and told her that I would like to appeal the BPO, which XXXX approved, but XXXX did not tell me about this appeal deadline, nor did she inform me of all of the requirements. When I requested to appeal, XXXX told me I just needed to provide it in writing. No other information was told to me, required of me, and I was informed it was being processed. Then more time passed. I figured it took so long to get the first BPO that I didnt expect this process to be fast either. After a while though I asked XXXX what was going on. She told me the appeal request was denied two days after it was processed and I was sent a letter, but that I would need to file a new appeal if I wanted it done. I informed her that I did not get a letter about the appeal denial, nor did she call me, email more or follow up in any sense. Annoyed, but just wanting to move on, I told her to provide me the denial letter and all the information I needed to submit so I could get it done asap. No Response. I followed up again, no response. Eventually, I was connected to XXXX XXXX, XXXX, as XXXX was not communicating. XXXX emailed to tell me the appeal deadline had passed, rudely said it was my fault, and not their problem if I didnt get the letter, and if I want to pay for a new BPO I could pay to do that but otherwise I was XXXX This email was an attempt to get me to look past their misconduct. Unfortunately for them, I know my rights from working at law firms, and having deadlines, necessary paperwork and details withheld for me is not within those rights. After much back and forth, I was finally provided the document I had supposedly been sent but I never received. However, this document showed me that my appeal was not in fact denied- it was denied pending that additional requirements be provided - the ones XXXX never informed me of before submitting my appeal, or afterwards. The same documents I could have, and would have, provided if I was informed they were needed. This document itself did not go into detail of what was necessary, and it also did not include a deadline for these pieces to be submitted for appeal. Even if I had received it, it would not have given me all relevant information needed to avoid missing the appeal deadline. Once I pointed out that no where on the letter did it say there was a 120-day deadline to appeal, or provide any mention of a deadline, in writing did they approve the new BPO. Of course they acted like they chose to do it for me out of generosity which couldnt be further from the truth. There were no good faith efforts put forth by XXXX. As I asked XXXX, how is one supposed to meet a deadline they are not informed of, or submit documentation they were not told were required? The answer is - one cant. I was set up for failure by Banner Bank employees, and then they continued to fail me once caught. That, to me, is unacceptable. Especially since it is very likely it is not just me this is happening to. If XXXX wasnt following up with me to see if I got everything, or still wanted to appeal, then she is probably not doing that for other clients. And XXXX, while not the one to make the original mistakes, made the situation go from bad to atrocious with her defensive and couldnt care less approach. XXXX lack of concern, or willingness to remedy, acknowledge or apologize for the fact that her team cost a client thousands in unnecessary payments, nor did she provide me the proper numbers or calculations- which I am stil waiting for since my first letter - mailed only- had incorrect numbers, and no calculations, regarding what my new monthly payment will be. The continued lack of attentiveness, and laziness, as well as XXXX XXXX XXXX behavior, is the reason I am opening this CFPB ticket. Not everyone is willing to stand up for themselves like I am and I worry how her bullying could harm others as it harmed me. XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX and knows banks so she was able to help advocate for me, but not everyone has that. Enough is enough. Having been a manager in legal, advocacy and customer service settings, I know the first step to making something right is to acknowledge the problem, empathize and offer something to make them feel better. Especially if it is something small for the business overall. This was not the approach taken, I was instead bullied, insulted, gaslit and robbed by XXXX and XXXX Banks actions. And I would like for them to remedy the damages instead of saying sucks to be you. In fact, XXXX exact words on the phone - before I was able to prove to her in writing that I was right and which got me the new BPO covered- were ummm yeah were not going to do any of those things you suggested because its not our fault, its yours. It was that moment that I decided I would stand up for myself, and others, who are being misled by these two random people who work for the bank. Especially since they are supposed to help us succeed, and the approach taken suggests it is not only me being taken advantage of. Other than my one phone call with XXXX, I made sure all communication was in writing so that I could document what was happening. To Preface this, the lender is well aware of the situation since I have persued legal action against them. By way of introduction theres a Department of Veteran Affairs document online ( VA Form 26-8978 ) that outlines certain rights that VA loan borrowers have, including that you may sell your home to someone who agrees to assume your loan if the loan holder or VA approves the creditworthiness of the purchaser ( s ). It also mentions that these rights apply to the borrower and, if you sell your home, to any buyer who assumes the loan. On XX/XX/2022, I signed a contract to assume a VA loan. In order to complete the assumption process we ( me the buyer and the sellers ) had to work with the loan holder or lender. The lender then made the determination that I was not credit worthy and denied the assumption on XX/XX/2022. The VA does have some safeguards in place meant to protect the sellers and buyers in my situation, or at least give us some recourse in the event the buyer is denied the assumption. In the Lenders Handbook - VA Pamphlet 26-7 Chapter 5.6.h. Decision Notices The VA mandates that in the event an assumption is disapproved the disapproval notice from the lender must include a notice that the lenders decision may be appealed to VA within 30 calendar days, This is a safeguard put in place by the VA to give an assumer a right to appeal, however unfortunately for me the lender never did give me the required notice that I could appeal their decision directly to the VA. As a result I was stuck, the lender refused to reconsider my application, and I had no idea I had the right to appeal the lender 's decision to the VA . Consequently, I lost the assumption deal and realized heavy financial loss along with opportunity cost due to the many months I spent working towards the assumption including trying to get the lender to follow the guidelines and grant me my rights therein which they failed or refused to do even after I pointed it out to them. I spent ~ {$30000.00} dollars pursuing litigation against the lender just to have a judge in Utah court rule that the lender had no duty towards me ( no duty in tort ( negligence ) for this relationship between Defendant and Plaintiff ) to follow the established VA guidelines. Thus my concerns are two fold, 1. If a lender can not be held accountable for not following guidelines meant to protect those transacting in VA loan assumptions then that puts the public at risk both civilian and veteran alike when pursuing VA loan assumptions from abuse of power by the lender, homes are big life changing deals/purchases. 2. I lost a lot of money, hopes, and dreams etc.. Due to the lender 's negligence, I am looking to recoup what I lost from the lender, to hold them accountable and set an example so that other lenders think twice about taking lightly or ignoring these guidelines. The Lender is Cross Country Mortgage, and the above is just a brief summary of the situation. They also took 49 days just to get us our assumption application, and violated other VA guidelines such as retaining the full {$300.00} + dollar processing fee when the guidelines specifically say to return {$50.00} in the event an assumption is not completed. etc.. And wrongly indicated to me that I needed to owner occupy the property in order to assume it. I have additional evidence detailing all my correspondence with the lender. Please reach out if you would like more information regarding my experience. The lender failed in their responsibilities throughout the whole process, chief among those is that the lender violated my rights by not notifying me of my right to appeal their decision to the VA.

Time and time again, financial firms negligent handling of consumer data in conjunction with a lack of basic information systems security results in data breaches. Without any accountability or penalties there is no incentive for adequate investment in security. Rather, costs saved by not implementing these basic measures fatten bottom lines while exposing consumers to immense risk and potential harm. It is incumbent upon the CFPB, FTC and other agencies to increase enforcement until the costs of a data breach become incentive to properly safeguard this sensitive information. It is also essential that notice of past breaches be made centrally available to inform consumers. This information would go a long way toward guiding consumers to firms that are capable and careful with their data as the paltry offers of credit monitoring are insufficient to redress the harm caused by this negligence.

As you can see from the above chain of documented events SNSC was in clear violation of Regulation X dual Track Foreclosure laws in that they were secretly scheduling the auction of this properly all the while giving us false and misleading information as if they were in fact negotiating with us in good faith. I would ask the court to impose severe sanctions against this servicer as a means to deter them from this illegal act to other homeowners. I would also ask for your honor to also order them to conduct a meaningful short sale review and to actually submit documents to the investor. The offer that was submitted to the SNSC was rejected and the SNSC agent indicated that they wanted an amount that was in excess of fair market value. Again XXXX XXXX advised that the offer would still be rejected without ever going back to the investor with that new higher offer amount. We have been processing this short sale in excess of the 30 or 35 days prior to the sale as required under dual track foreclosure laws. Regulation X, implemented by the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ( CFPB ) pursuant to the Real Estate Settlement Procedure Act ( RESPA ), governs the handling of mortgage servicing, including loss mitigation and foreclosure proceedings. It establishes certain rights and responsibilities for both borrowers and servicers, with the objective of promoting fair and transparent practices in the mortgage industry. RESPA supersedes state law via the Supremacy Clause of the United States. Section 1024.41 of Regulation X specifically addresses the procedures and requirements for evaluating and responding to borrowers loss mitigation applications. It stipulates that once a complete application is received, the servicer must acknowledge the receipt in writing within five business days. Furthermore, the servicer is required to exercise reasonable diligence in obtaining all necessary documents and evaluating the application for a loss mitigation option. During this review process, foreclosure proceedings, including the scheduling of an auction date must be stayed. These actions by SNSC SERVICING is the textbook scenario why Dual Track Foreclosure laws were enacted. To stop banks from selling a homeowners home while at the same time reviewing them for work out options. The failure to cancel the auction and to complete the short sale review directly contradicts the spirit and intent of Regulation X, which aims to provide homeowners with a fair opportunity to explore loss mitigation options before facing the dire consequences of a foreclosure auction. I write this letter in a good faith attempt to have the foreclosure auction date removed and for the short sale to be reviewed again in a fair and amicable manner

In XXXX vs XXXX, the XXXX held that the XXXX XXXX 's findings of fact were supported by competent evidence and that as a matter of law, " A party to a contract may not complain of the nonperformance of the other party where that performance is prevented by his own actions. A party can not take advantage of a condition precedent the performance of which he has rendered impossible. A party who deliberately prevents the fulfillment of a condition on which his liability under a contract depends can not take advantage of his own conduct and claim that the failure of the fulfillment of the condition defeats his liability. Delays and nonperformance while they amount to a failure to perform are excused where performance is prevented by the other party to the contract. XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX XXXX. On XXXX XXXX, XXXX, I applied for a cash-out refinance from Wells Fargo XXXX I have banked with Wells Fargo for 23 years. At the time I applied, I owed approximately {$8000.00} on a first mortgage with a different lender and had no other liens on my property. I requested a {$120000.00} cash-out refinance. I told the first loan officer I spoke with, XXXX XXXX, that I was requesting the refinance for the purposes of home improvement and to pay off debt. I told her I needed to repair my roof which was original to the house and XXXX XXXX XXXX. Wells Fargo required me to pay for my appraisal upfront, a total of {$990.00}. I was told this amount was not refundable after the appraisal had taken place. I paid Wells Fargo this amount. I was conditionally approved for the cash-out refinance on XXXX XXXX. I produced every one of a multitude of documents requested by Wells Fargo, including reams of documents from the local auditor 's office required to satisfy underwriters that I had recorded well , road maintenance and easement agreements. Many documents Wells Fargo required were private and requesting them seemed intrusive, but having had a XXXX relationship with Wells and knowing they already had access to my bank records, I provided the documents as requested and hoped for the best. I spent many hours researching and providing the requested documents. Despite my need for a new roof, my homeowners insurance agreed to rewrite my policy at Wells Fargo 's ( repeated ) request ( Wells contacted my insurance agency multiple times about this, something my agent said was unusual ) to provide 100 % wind and hail coverage. The newly-issued policy showed Wells as loss payee and was sent to Wells Fargo . Wells Fargo knew I had adequate homeowners insurance coverage. I sent loan officers copies of my contract for a new roof scheduled to be replaced XXXX XXXX, XXXX, along with receipts showing I had made a good faith down payment. As promised, my roof has now been replaced, as of XX/XX/XXXX. The appraisal took place on XXXX XXXX. The appraiser appraised my home at {$710000.00}, despite noting that I needed a new roof, that a beam beneath my upper deck had rotted and needed to be replaced, and that the siding on my home " should be checked '' although issues with my siding, he said, were " cosmetic. '' The appraiser also noted I needed a second strap on my water heater and a plug-in carbon monoxide detector, the latter two items costing less than {$100.00}. The appraiser estimated that replacing the roof, staining the siding and replacing the beam in the deck would cost approximately {$30000.00}. Wells Fargo then told me that I would have to complete all repairs before my loan could close. Loan officers told me underwriting suggested that I ask the contractors to agree to complete the work but to wait to be paid from the title company after all of the work was completed. Wells Fargo also told me that all of the work done would have to be inspected at my expense. I told Wells Fargo that in the XXXX XXXX, siding can not be stained or painted until summertime because weather conditions do not allow for it. Their requirement meant that I would have to ask roofers and the deck contractor to do their work but wait until summer, six months away or longer, to be paid. My application was sent to underwriters for a secondary review. The new underwriters agreed that all of the work would have to be completed and inspected before my loan could close. It is not reasonable to ask roofers and other contractors to perform work for which they can not be paid for six months or longer in order to await weather conditions favorable for painting.The appraiser did not state that the siding on my house was damaged, dangerous or deficient, only that it should be " looked at '' because of " cosmetic '' issues, yet Wells was stating that closing of my loan hinged on the siding being stained. I applied for a comparatively small mortgage, {$120000.00}, on a house appraised at {$710000.00}, even with needed roof and other repairs. I satisfied all of Wells Fargo 's requests for information and had a conditional loan approval. I have a long relationship with Wells Fargo. I have no overdrafts to my checking account and have never been late on a Wells Fargo credit card payment. I do not have a single late payment on my credit report. I provided evidence to loan officers that my roof was scheduled for replacement. I am now out countless hours of research and negotiations along with {$990.00} for this appraisal. I have had my privacy invaded also. Wells Fargo should tell applicants upfront when they are applying for a cash-out refinance for the purpose of home improvement that their underwriters may require necessary repairs and inspections for which they will be required to pay before any loan will close. Failing to disclose this information seems deceptive and misleading. At the very least, Wells Fargo should include appraisal and inspection fees in closing costs and not require them upfront before closing.

So when I closed, I was required to fund my escrow account with a much higher amount than I would ever really need. But I knew Id eventually get some of it back once the loan provider could see what my bills actually would be. My mortgage broker advised me to contact the loan service company XXXX Rocket Mortgage ) once I received my first property tax bill so they could do an escrow analysis so that I could hopefully get a refund and reduce my future monthly escrow payments. I received my first tax bill in the beginning of XXXX. Ill note that it seemed a little odd to me that it was addressed to the previous owner, but I didn't think that mattered, as it was a tax bill for XXXX, and it clearly showed the property taxes that were owed. By this point, I knew that my escrow account was scheduled for analysis in XX/XX/XXXX, but I was hoping to speed up the process by a month or XXXX, so I called Rocket Mortgage. The man I spoke to was very helpful. He suggested I upload the bill and then call back in a few days to make sure it had been received. At that point, they could request an escrow analysis. And then life happened and before I knew it, it was XXXX and I hadn't had a chance to call back yet. In that time, I had received another tax bill that was actually in my name, and had the same amounts due. But I didn't think that it would matter, since it was all the same info, minus my name, so I filed the bill away and forgot about it. In that time, Rocket Mortgage had also made my first property tax payment, so they clearly had accurate data on how much I was actually paying. At the beginning of XXXX, I finally called Rocket Mortgage back. They confirmed that they had received the property tax bill that Id uploaded and that they would move forward with an escrow analysis. The woman I spoke to, XXXX, estimated that I'd have a refund by the end of the month and reduced monthly escrow payments by XXXX. She mentioned nothing about the property tax bill I sent having the name of the previous owner. XXXX turned to XXXX, and I had seen no progress on the Rocket Mortgage website regarding my escrow account. On XX/XX/XXXX, I called again to check in and spoke to XXXX. He confirmed that they were still researching my property tax situation, which at this point was a little confusing to me why they had to research. They clearly had my property tax payment info, since they had already made XXXX payment in XXXX. But I didn't question him further on the topic. He also confirmed that my annual analysis was scheduled for XXXX, so it basically was going to coincide with the research that was already happening. He said to give it another week or so. He mentioned nothing about the tax bill I had submitted in XXXX having the name of the previous owner. On XX/XX/XXXX, I finally saw that my escrow analysis had been completed. Yay! I was getting a refund... but not as big as I had been expecting And when I started looking at the actual report, I realized that my monthly escrow payments were not changing. And the amount they were estimating I'd pay in property taxes had not changed at all. Now I was really confused. Even if I hadn't uploaded a copy of my property tax bill to them, they had paid my property tax bill in XXXX, so they clearly were getting information directly from my county on how much to pay. And if they had that info, how could they still think that my taxes would still be just shy of {$6000.00}?? I called Rocket Mortgage that day and talked to XXXX. It was a very confusing conversation. She seemed to be saying that they had no evidence that my taxes would be less, and therefore I had to wait another year for another analysis for things to be figured out. This is when I started to get angry. She was basically telling me that on top of Rocket Mortgage holding onto thousands of dollars of excess money in my escrow account, I would be required to pay hundreds of dollars more per month for another year until Rocket Mortgage could figure it out. This was completely contradictory to everything Id been told before. And it also seemed not legal. From the little that I understand about Escrow accounts, there are laws in place that limit how much can be held in an escrow account. But by the end, it seemed that the issue was that I had submitted the property tax bill with the previous owner 's name. Which, again, confused me because Rocket had already paid my property tax bill in XXXX, so they could already see that my payments were going to be much less than they had been estimating. I told XXXX that I would upload the proper bill with my name that evening. She said she would call me in a day or so to follow up. In retrospect, yes, it logically makes sense that I should have not sent in the bill with the previous owner 's name because her taxes wouldn't necessarily correspond to what I would owe. But this is the first property I have purchased, and I'm learning. I don't know everything. And Rocket Mortgage had multiple chances to inform me that they needed the bill with my name. Yet it wasnt until I talked to XXXX, more than XXXX months after I had first initially contacted them, and after the analysis had been completed, that I was told that they didnt have what they needed. I uploaded the proper bill that evening. It was a holiday weekend, so I called the following Tuesday, XX/XX/XXXX, to confirm that they had received the bill. The man I spoke to, XXXX, said they had received it. I missed a call from XXXX the next day XX/XX/XXXX. She left a message saying that she had an update and if I called back, anyone I talked to would have the update. I called and spoke to XXXX. He could find no record of a note from XXXX about an update. He said hed get in touch with her and give me a call back. He called me the next day, XX/XX/XXXX. He said that the update was simply that they had received the property tax bill. All looked good. And they were moving forward with an additional escrow analysis. I asked him what the timeframe would be for the process. He said it would take XXXX business days, so Id probably hear back the following week. I didnt hear anything the entire following week, and on XX/XX/XXXX, I received an email saying that my loan was being transferred to XXXX XXXX XXXX I called Rocket Mortgage the following Monday for an update and spoke with XXXX. I was hoping he would say that everything would be figured out before the loan was transferred. But instead, he basically told me that Id have to deal with it with XXXX. He reiterated that an analysis would take XXXX business days, so even if they started the analysis today it wouldnt get done in time. So, apparently, despite XXXX different people telling me the analysis had started, it had in fact not been started at all. And now I was stuck having to start the whole process over again with a new loan servicer. I fully understand that I did not provide the correct document in the beginning, but Rocket Mortgage had many chances to inform me that they needed a different document. And furthermore, I am still very confused about how Rocket Mortgage can still think my property taxes would be close to {$6000.00} for the year when the last payment they made for me in XX/XX/XXXX was around {$750.00}. Something that should have taken weeks has now dragged out into months. In the meantime, Rocket Mortgage has been holding onto an excess amount of money in my escrow account. And Ive had to pay hundreds of dollars more for XXXX, and now probably XXXX too since I dont have high hopes that XXXX will be any quicker in figuring this all out. Ownership of houses frequently extends to multiple individuals, similar to home mortgages. The allowance of co-signers for personal and car loans is common practice, with solar loans often paralleling mortgages. Yet, Dividend Finance has chosen to deviate from industry norms, crafting policies that exclusively benefit the lender at the expense of all other transactional parties. My four-year ordeal with Dividend Finance reveals a company indifferent to consumer grievances. While the company may argue that these policies streamline processes and mitigate default risks, efficiency can not be pursued solely for the lender 's benefit. Should Dividend Finance persist in its current practices without considering consumers or the broader implications, federal intervention becomes imperative to dictate appropriate conduct. Despite proclamations of environmental commitment and a " customer-centric '' ethos, Dividend Finance 's actions betray a cold indifference towards those it purports to serve, focusing solely on securing monthly interest payments without concern for its impact. The company 's mission to " improve the outcome for everyone involved '' rings hollow, resembling nothing more than a public relations facade.

On the other hand, they proceeded to add unjustified fees to our loan, not process our payments, ignore the payments that were made following the guidelines established for XXXX XXXXXXXX by the United States Bankruptcy Code, request unnecessary information, in some cases starting foreclosures, and also not respond to our emails or phone calls when we tried to figure out what was happening. We haven't received any assistance or it was denied for the loan we have with 21st Mortgage Corporation. Additionally, the monthly mortgage statements show a constant increase in the amounts without any fair reason. Below is a summary of the facts : On XX/XX/XXXX, we received an email from XXXX responding to our request for Loss Mitigation, so they sent us a letter of acknowledgment of receipt from 21st Mortgage Corporation, where they requested the following documents : 1 ) Fully completed and executed Loss Mitigation Application ( this may also be completed over the phone ). 2 ) If you have a short sale offer on the property, a copy of the Listing Agreement with your Realtor ( if applicable ), a payoff of any junior liens ( if applicable ), a copy of the Purchase Agreement with the Buyer, Buyers Proof of Funds or Lender Pre-Approval for the purchase, and a copy of the HUD-1 Settlement Statement or Closing Disclosure if you have an offer. Consequently, we answered their reaching out to us and also attached the application form filled out. Then on XX/XX/XXXX, they requested our bankruptcy case number and we sent them our Bankruptcy case file to the email of XXXX, the same day we received an email from them asking if the primary borrower was the owner of XXXX XXXX XXXX. On XX/XX/XXXX we tried to get in contact with them to make sure that all of our taxes and insurance were escrowed on all loans, because we werent able to get insurance, since the homes won't pass inspections due to hurricanes. On XX/XX/XXXX, we sent to XXXX our Loss Mitigation Application for the property address at XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX Then on the XXXX, we received a response to that email saying that our application was going to be submitted for review. On the XXXX we sent another email to them to explain that it was a mistake with the application form attached the previous day, so we proceeded to attach an updated one with the list of monthly expenses, therefore the same day they responded that they understood and they were going to pass this along to the loss mitigation department. On XX/XX/XXXX we sent a letter to XXXX and XXXX stating that in XXXX we were impacted by 2 hurricanes back-to-back, on XX/XX/XXXX, by hurricane Ian and on XX/XX/XXXX, by hurricane Nicole and also state that we've been calling ever since to get loan assistance and we have gotten no solution because we wanted to keep the property and being current with the loan. Additionally, we asked about the requirements we need to provide to apply and we addressed that we wanted to make sure that all of our taxes and insurance were escrowed on our loan. We explained to them that any insurance would insure the property due to the extensive number of hurricanes in the state of Florida. In addition to this, on the same date, we sent an email with the information we previously mentioned to XXXX We believe that our payment processes have been marred by irregularities, undue delays, and unfair decisions made by the Mortgage XXXX. As we can prove to you, we have always fulfilled our commitments to them in each loan and we are willing to continue doing so, despite the adverse impact of COVID-19 and Hurricane Ian on XXXX XXXX XXXX Although 21st Mortgage Corporation is not a licensed mortgage lender in Florida State, it is committed to compliance with the Loan Originators and Mortgage Brokers Chapter 494, Title XXXIII of the Florida Statutes ( XXXX ), and at this time we consider that they didnt obey legal obligations established for lenders under federal and state laws in case of natural disasters. According to the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau and the Florida Office of Financial Regulation, these obligations aim to protect borrowers from financial hardship caused by the disaster. Some of the key legal obligations of lenders during and after a natural disaster are : 1. Mortgage Forbearance : The Coronavirus Aid, Relief, and Economic Security ( CARES ) Act enacted by Congress in XX/XX/XXXX provides mortgage forbearance for federally-backed mortgages for up to 18 months due to COVID-19-related financial hardships. This forbearance applies to natural disasters as well. Lenders must provide borrowers with a forbearance period of at least 90 days for federally-backed mortgages and up to 180 days for non-federally-backed mortgages. During the forbearance period, lenders can not charge late fees, report late payments to credit bureaus, or initiate foreclosure proceedings. At this point, we never received at least 90 days of mortgage forbearance, otherwise, we continued receiving charges for late fees and also the increase in our mortgage statements, which made it even more difficult to cover our responsibilities. 2. Disaster Assistance : Lenders must provide borrowers with information about disaster assistance programs offered by federal, state, and local agencies. This information must be provided in writing and in a language that the borrower understands. Lenders must also provide borrowers with a list of resources that can help them recover from the disaster. 3. Communication : Lenders must communicate clearly and frequently with borrowers about their options during and after the disaster. This communication must be in a language that the borrower understands and must include information about forbearance, disaster assistance, and any other available resources. About points XXXX and XXXX, it is important to state that although we receive communications from 21st Mortgage Corporation when we request mortgage assistance, they request some information but they never continue with the application process. Otherwise, multiple times we tried to get in contact with them but we always received excuses or when we received a communication from them it was a negative one with no fair motivation. 4. Modification of Loan Terms : Lenders may modify loan terms for borrowers affected by the disaster. These modifications may include extending the loan term, reducing the interest rate, or deferring payments. Lenders must provide borrowers with written notice of any loan modifications. In addition to this point, we never managed the possibility of having a loan terms modification, otherwise, we saw how the interest rates increase month by month along with the late payments fees.

My general problem is that my mortgage was sold without my consent to a different mortgage company ( Mr. Cooper ). I am dissatisfied with the service provided by this new company, but I can't just change to a different company. My only choice is to re-finance with a new company and incur the costs associated with that transaction along with a potentially much higher interest rate. Also, there's no guarantee that my newly refinanced mortgage wouldn't simply be sold right back to the same company I'm dissatisfied with. This leaves all the power in the hands of giant financial institutions and leaves consumers like me with no choices at all. Most home owners in the US are just like me and my husband : we have one mortgage on our primary place of residence. This represents our largest single investment. Yet we have zero choice once closing documents are signed as to what company will continue to service our mortgage. Average consumers should have more control over who services their mortgage than faceless corporations we've never heard of who provide poor service.

text: My husband and I bought a new home in XX/XX/XXXX. It was a brand new community and we knew the house would not be ready until XX/XX/XXXX. We are XXXX XXXX that were relocated to XXXX XXXX NV for my husband 's work. It is important to note that this is our first time buying a house in the United States and the buying process is very different in XXXX. Over the next year we travelled to XXXX XXXX a few times to see the house and to make our selections. We sold our home in XXXX in order to invest our profits as a down payment on our home in XXXX XXXX. It was always clear that even though we were on a temporary visa that allowed us to be in the US, we were permanently relocating with our young children. We were referred to a lender by the builder which we worked with. Throughout the purchasing process we were asked to complete numerous different forms in order to qualify for a mortgage and to provide a gamete of documents as proof of funds. At the beginning of the process, we were asked to complete a Uniform Residential Loan Application ( URLA ). Months went by as the house was being built. I spoke to our lender in XX/XX/XXXX where I asked numerous questions about the lending process. XXXX of the questions I asked was about refinancing our mortgage as we were purchasing our home at a time when rates were quite high. The lender confirmed that there are no penalties for refinancing. *I have my personal handwritten notes from this call. Over the summer of XXXX we sold our home in XXXX, packed up our belongings and were ready to move to our new home. Once our home was officially sold in XXXX we were asked to provide proof of funds as well as confirmation of our final numbers ; which we provided. Keeping in mind that the profits from the sale of our home had to be converted to US dollars as well as wired to our US account. We provided all documents that were requested and had sufficient funds to close on the house. Our closing date was set for XX/XX/XXXX. We asked our lender when we would know our final numbers for our monthly mortgage payments. We were told that we would only know the final numbers once we sign at the title company. It is important to note that we do not know the process of buying a home in the US and nothing was explained to us. We asked what a title company was, what did escrow mean, and numerous questions around insurance. We also asked why we needed an appraisal, everything was new for us. Finally on XX/XX/XXXX I received a text message from our lender that we would be receiving a XXXX of the last disclosures. Upon reviewing these documents I texted the lender advising that the dates on the document were not correct and asked when we would be going over the numbers ( monthly payments, fees, insurance ect. ) We were told the date can be changed if funding goes smoothly and that we need to sign the documents due to a 3 day recission period and that if we were trying to close on time for the XXXX, they need the signed documents asap. We felt pressured to sign the documents right away as we were living in a hotel with our kids and dog waiting to move to our new home. We were still asking at this point when we would be receiving information about our home insurance, and asking how much the insurance was going to cost. We were never explained any of the financial numbers, we were told by the lender that all this would be done at the signing at the title company. Regarding our insurance the text message said that our insurance policy was done as an investment property due to our type of loan and that as soon as we close they would email the insurance agent to have him change it to a primary. I confirmed by text again that once we close this would be changed to primary and asked if we needed mortgage insurance. We were asking these questions the day before we were to sign at the title company, clearly feeling uninformed. We later discovered that we were sold tenant insurance! The lender asked us on XX/XX/XXXX by email to print, sign and date the Intent to Proceed with the date of : XX/XX/XXXX and return it to them as they had received the wrong form from the investor as they were supposed to have been sent XXXX in the initial disclosures in XX/XX/XXXX. This is another example of the lender not being honest and not acting in our best interests. The next day, on XX/XX/XXXX we arrived for our appointment at the title company. We are anxious for numerous reasons but also because we wanted to understand our numbers. As we were signing document after document I told my husband, I don't even know what we're signing. I asked the person who was having us sign the documents why the documents say that this is an investment property and I asked them when we would be getting to the final numbers and when they would be explaining the numbers to us. They informed us that this is not done at title and that that is done with our lender and that we could call them if we wanted to. We called them and they were on the phone so we texted them and asked them why our property is documented as an investment property when this is not an investment property, this is our primary home. We received a text back stating that this is the type of loan we had to get in order to have us approved and that they used the rental income to offset the mortgage to qualify. It was either that or a foreign national with a foreign national rate so both are done as investment properties. I then replied asking what rental income? They responded with the market rental income from appraisal. At this point, we were signing documents we clearly had never been explained, we had no idea what was going on and I was physically not feeling well because we did not understand what was going on. This was never an investment, this was and still is our primary home. We never had any intentions on purchasing this home for an investment. When we had seen the term investment in the documents prior to arriving at the title company we thought the term 'investment ' was referred to as home ownership in the US - an investment. We did not realize that this was a type of loan or loan program. XX/XX/XXXX was our closing date. We found out that afternoon that we would not be able to close from the builder. Our lender never told us! We reached out to them and asked when they were going to tell us we were not closing that day and they apologized as they were in training and did not have access to their phone. Our property is registered with the county treasurer as our primary home, we signed a document at closing from our HOA confirming that this was our primary home and that we would be living there and we told our lender that this was our primary home and confirmed this on our URLA. About a month ago we started to look into refinancing our mortgage as we have a very high interest rate. As we were about to have our mortgage paid by a new lender, we were advised that there was a prepayment penalty of {$18000.00}. We had no idea there was a penalty as we had been told there was not going to be one. Due to our current loan we have a prepayment penalty if we want to refinance within the next 3 years! On XX/XX/XXXX I called the investor in order to confirm the prepayment penalty as this was the first time I was hearing of this. I asked them how this was possible and that we were needing to refinance to a better interest rate. They advised that it was not likely possible for me to get a better rate in this market. I advised them that I had secured a better rate of 1.75 % less than what we currently have. I was told that I should jump on it then ; which is a horrible thing to tell someone that you just confirmed to that they are locked into an {$18000.00} prepayment penalty. We have since sent an email on XX/XX/XXXX requesting our initial disclosures and loan application and followed up on XX/XX/XXXX and have still never received a response. It is clear that we were never explained anything about our loan or the loan program, we never once met with our lender. We were taken advantage of because we are foreign and no due diligence was done with our loan. Above our prepayment penalty we incurred additional expenses on our home appraisal as there was a need for extra forms to compare rental income in the area. We do not feel that the lender or the investor did their due diligence on our file and we were taken advantage of and put into a terrible situation. No one reviewed our file for accuracy or compliance. This is a clear case of occupancy fraud. Our lender knew beyond a shadow of a doubt that this was our primary home, NOT an investment property. They then locked us into a program for an investment property with a massive prepayment penalty. We were put in a predatory lending situation as we asked for explanations of costs and our insurance numerous times which were met with silence. I have text messages as well as emails and documents to confirm everything that I have mentioned in my complaint is factual. A prepayment penalty of over XXXX XXXX dollars is a massive financial hardship to have to pay off just to refinance to a lower rate. The lender was aware that we would be refinancing as soon as we could due to our high interest rate. We were not treated fairly or responsibly by the lender or the investor. We are concerned on how to approach this situation because of not knowing the lending process we also do not know how to complaint process works. We are simply looking for assistance and a friend referred us to CFPB because the lender and the company we are making payments to are both of no help and have been brushing us off and we are urgently needing help. We are requesting for our situation to be reviewed and investigated because we would be horrified if this was happening to others as well and feel it is only right to report what has happened to me and my family. We are now in a horrible payment and fraudulent program and would like this to be rectified as soon as possible. The lender knowingly forced us into a fraudulent situation. We have not been able to get anywhere with the lender or the investor and this is why we are reaching out to the CFPB for help because this is the only other hope we have in getting some resolution to this tragic situation. Thank you,

She further stated the process takes less than 10 minutes, so I requested a new COE and provided an updated copy to the loan processor immediately. I made multiple attempts to speak with my loan processor to ensure we provided all of the information needed but was unable to contact her by phone, so I sent an email. Furthermore, a credit report was conducted on my husband in XXXX per VA requirements. The underwriters were able to calculate his debt and bring up previous addresses that were calculated into their decision. I provided all of the requested documents but I refuse to write another letter of explanation for questions that have already been answered in previous submittals and for questions that do not regard my financial standing.

Thus the claim of BAC on XXXX XXXX of the Foreclosure Deed that it owned the Promissory Note is a falsity and without basis. As such, the Foreclosure Deed on XX/XX/XXXX in NULL and VOID. Assignment of Mortgage The Assignment of Mortgage recorded on XX/XX/XXXX had XXXX pages. Page XXXX and XXXX indicate the Agreement for Signing Authority between XXXX XXXX, ( XXXX ), its subsidiary MERS, Countrywide as Member and XXXX & XXXX XXXX. ( XXXX ) as Vendor, this is the law firm that appeared to have allowed its employees to be certifying officers for MERS. ( See attachment : Assignment of Mortgage ). This Agreement for Signing Authority section was dated around XXXX and XX/XX/XXXX or XXXX years before this Assignment of Mortgage on XX/XX/XXXX. This indicates that if might have been a boilerplate form previously used elsewhere XXXX years prior. It should be pointed out that XXXX has NO ( XXXX ) employees and its parent company XXXX, in a deposition, admitted to having XXXX employees. And yet at XXXX point they are the mortgagee of record on XXXX XXXX mortgages - again with XXXX employees. So through agreement for signing authority they have appointed XXXX people as certifying officers ( based on a testimony of XXXX XXXX XXXX of XXXX ) with essentially no checks, limitations or restrictions that are monitored on the activities of these so-called certifying officers which has resulted in thousands of foreclosure fraud and abuses. XXXX XXXX of Appointing Officers is Outside the Law The Alabama Supreme Court on the case of XXXX XXXX XXXX ( No. XXXX dated XX/XX/XXXX ) ruled on XXXX XXXX that XXXX system of appointing agents is outside the law. ( See Attachment : XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX ) The portion of AL Supreme Court ruling on this appointing of agents as outside the law reads in part : XXXX XXXXXXXX XXXX system of appointing agents is outside the law. Thousands of people are authorized to act as certifying officers of XXXX. ( XXXX XXXX ). This term of art has no legal meaning under Alabama law. XXXX XXXX, the CEO for MERS, testified his company has authority to foreclose because of the limited authority of these thousands of certifying officers. ( XXXX XXXX ) and even testified in front of a XXXX XXXX studying this issue that XXXX has granted XXXX people certifying XXXX status. ( XXXX XXXX XXXX on XXXX XXXX XXXX ). According to XXXX, XXXX provides its members a corporate resolution designating XXXX or more employees of the member as a certifying XXXX. ( XXXX XXXX ). Certifying officers are given authority to act in XXXX areas on behalf of MERS. ( XXXX XXXX ). But nothing in the documentation provided by XXXX indicates that any certifying officer has or had accurate knowledge of the transfers of XXXX loan. XXXX employee XXXX testified that while he XXXX was a certifying XXXX of XXXX, he did not know exactly what criteria was used to authorize him as a certifying officer or what steps were taken. Instead, he received an email from MERS announcing that he was now a XXXX officer. ( XXXX XXXX ). XXXX XXXX never filled out an application and never filed an affidavit to become a XXXX certifying officer. ( XXXX XXXX ). The XXXX resolution from XXXX to XXXX appointing certifying officers, along with the XXXX supplement granting authority to each of the XXXX different legal entities XXXX Mortgage operates under, is vague. What appears to take place is that MERS, an entity that is a nominee of XXXX, gives XXXX a blank slate upon which to write any of its employees it chooses to act on MERS 's behalf. In effect, MERS and XXXX have turned principal/agent law on its head : XXXX, an agent of XXXX, XXXX XXXX the XXXX to act as an agent on its behalf. If both XXXX and XXXX are the agent and the principal, then who is accountable when there is a violation of law? An agent is presumed to intend to bind his principal only and to incur no personal liability and unless an intention to substitute or super add his personal liability for or to that of his principal is clearly shown, XXXX he will not be bound in his individual capacity. XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX ( XXXX ). XXXX argues it is not an agent, but simply a nominee of XXXX. A nominee is generally understood as a person designated to act in place of another. See XXXX 's XXXX XXXX ( XXXX XXXX ). But, how can MERS acting in place of XXXX XXXX XXXX 's action in the appointing of certifying officers? Again, XXXX is attempting to stand XXXX letter law on its head. Certification of XXXX XXXX XXXX, an employee of XXXX, of the Assignment of Mortgage is invalid, outside the law, and therefore null and void Thus, based on this important Alabama Supreme Court ruling, the signature of XXXX XXXX XXXX, an employee of XXXX is outside the law and therefore null and void. No consideration specified in the assignment of mortgage The existence of consideration in contracts or exchange of property is critical to its legality. What was the consideration? I have absolutely no confidence in their abilities to comply with banking regulations, and can only imagine the time, effort, and frustration that would go into trying to recoup funds that they inevitably would incorrectly debit from my account in error if I had signed a form allowing them to do so. So, on XX/XX/XXXX, I directed XXXX to send the check via XXXX to my new address, provided the new address, and asked that she provide me with the XXXX tracking number as soon as the check was mailed. '' Unsurprisingly, that was the last I heard from XXXX, despite two additional follow-up emails sent to her. text: Hello my name is XXXX XXXX I am the Biological Heir of XXXX XXXX my XXXX died with out will I was contacted by chase mortgage about his death and his estate I contacted them with his Death certificate and my birth certificate to show that he was my biological father and chase mortgage decided to sell property after I sent them the information about his death i updated and instead of following state and federal statue codes they sold or pre foreclosed on property by using a third party debt collector who filed for a auction for property then the they talked to XXXX child about XXXX XXXX account Federal Act I the right to sell house His wife had will for her she was not co signer on XXXX XXXX Mortgage so property inherited by the next of kin when I called the bank would only talk to step child and sent pay off quote to step child The federal act they broke was GarnSt Germain Act they never let me take over payments Key Provisions of the Act Right to privacy act The Garn St. Germain Act addressed due-on-sale clauses in mortgage contracts. These clauses allowed lenders to demand full repayment when a property changed hands. The Act recognized these clauses as enforceable but introduced critical exceptions for specific situations. One major exception involved property inheritance. When a family member inherits a property, they can continue the deceaseds mortgage payments without refinancing. This exception is vital for heirs who might not qualify for a new loan. Another exception concerns joint tenants. It allows property owners to add certain family members, like a spouse or child, to the property title without triggering the mortgages full repayment. The Act also supports estate planning. It allows property transfers into a certain type of trust without demanding loan repayment. This is crucial for managing assets and avoiding probate. Many individuals plan to avoid the complicated and public probate process through an inter vivos trust. Also called a revocable living trust, this legal tool allows for a more accessible estate administration process for your loved ones. In North Carolina, these provisions streamline real estate transactions involving inherited properties. They provide clarity and financial relief for families during the transfer of ownership. Understanding these key provisions helps heirs and property owners plan effectively. It ensures smooth transitions in property ownership and mortgage responsibilities. You can read more about what the act did for the average American at XXXX or talk with an experienced estate planning attorney.

Background : Our property hazard insurance with XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX expired on XX/XX/XXXX. We did not receive the written notice required under Colorado statute, leaving us with little time to secure replacement coverage as required by the terms of the Deed of Trust under our loan agreement ( " LA '' ) with Wells Fargo Bank , N.A . ( " WF '' ). Further complicating the process of securing replacement coverage is the current perceived wildfire risk throughout Colorado, which has resulted in lack of available coverage from any carriers in more than 50 % of the state, including in the area in which our property is located. We received an initial notice of lack of evidence of insurance coverage from WF on XX/XX/XXXX stating, in part, " Because hazard insurance is required on your property, we plan to buy insurance for your property '', clearly indicating that XXXX had not yet purchased such coverage. We bound replacement coverage effective XX/XX/XXXX and provided this information to Wells Fargo on XX/XX/XXXX. We received confirmation of receipt of proof of coverage from WF on XX/XX/XXXX, with additional commentary stating, in part, " Our records show that there was a lapse in coverage from XX/XX/XXXX to XX/XX/XXXX. An insurance charge of {$2600.00} may be charged to your account for the period of time that the coverage was in force. In order to avoid this charge or have it reversed from your account; please provide us with evidence of insurance for this lapse period. '' On XX/XX/XXXX, we provided a No Loss Letter to WF which certifies that no losses occurred during the lapse period, memorializing the fact that there are no losses to insure against during the lapse period. Page 5, section 5, paragraph two of the LA states, in part, " If Borrower fails to maintain any of the coverages described above, Lender may obtain insurance coverage, at Lender 's option and Borrower 's expense. ". As evidence of insurance was provided to WF on XX/XX/XXXX and subsequent correspondence from WF dated XX/XX/XXXX indicates that WF had not yet obtained coverage at Borrower 's expense, the above language in Section 5 of the LA should prohibit WF from obtaining coverage at Borrower 's expense " after '' evidence of coverage has been provided. In addition to the foregoing, page 5, section 5, paragraph two of the LA further states " Any amounts disbursed by Lender under this Section 5 shall become additional debt of Borrower secured by this Security Instrument. '' On XX/XX/XXXX, we received a copy of the declarations for an insurance policy " purportedly '' taken out by WF. The declarations show an effective date of XX/XX/XXXX and an annual premium in the amount of {$46000.00}. The bottom right corner of the policy declarations notes a policy issue date of XX/XX/XXXX. There is no evidence of any amounts actually " disbursed '' by WF as is required under the terms of the LA. Our latest mortgage statement, dated XX/XX/XXXX, now shows an escrow balance of ( {$2600.00} ), with interest being charged at 3.125 % per annum. As WF 's correspondence history and the declarations page for the policy which WF purportedly took out both clearly indicate that it did not obtain coverage until " after '' we had provided evidence of coverage, WF has no exposure for the lapse period pursuant to the No Loss Letter provided to WF, and further WF has failed to provide proof of any amounts actually disbursed by WF, it is our position that WF has breached the terms of the LA on multiple points. We have attempted to discuss this matter with the appropriate personnel at WF via telephone on numerous occasions and have repeatedly been denied contact information for anyone in the department which administers the insurance coverage requirements under WF 's loan agreements. As such, we are respectfully requesting the CFPB 's assistance in resolving this matter. Additionally, our credit report now shows an increase in debt outstanding due to WF reporting the escrow balance as new debt, which has negatively impacted our credit score. We are requesting CFPB 's assistance on this matter as well. Finally, WF 's website now shows our current insurance policy as having an effective date of XX/XX/XXXX and an expiration date of XX/XX/XXXX. This is inaccurate as our current policy, which WF has previously acknowledged both receiving and accepted ( and reflected same on its insurance verification portal ), has an effective date of XX/XX/XXXX and an expiration date of XX/XX/XXXX. As we have been prevented from speaking with anyone at WF about these matters, we are requesting CFPB 's intervention on this matter as well. Thank you very much for your prompt attention to this matter, and please let us know if any additional information may be required to assist in your efforts.

text: Dear LoanCare, As servicer of our mortgage loan, LoanCare shall treat this as both a Notice of Error pursuant to the Real Estate Settlement Procedures Act ( RESPA ), subject to the response period set out in Regulation X, 12 C.F.R. 1024.35 ( b ) ( 1 ) - ( 11 ), and as a Request for Information pursuant to Sections 1024.35 and 1024.36 ( d ) ( 2 ) ( i ) ( B ). In XX/XX/XXXX, the XXXX issued several final rules to address the systemic problems in the mortgage servicing industry to implement protections for borrowers with regard to mortgage servicing. These new rules amended 12 C.F.R. Part 1024, RESPA ( Regulation X ), and became effective on XX/XX/XXXX. Notably, under RESPA, [ l ] oss mitigation option means any alternative to foreclosure offered by the owner or assignee of a mortgage loan that is made available through the servicer to the borrower. 12 C.F.R. 1024.31. This definition was intended to be expansive, encompassing not just loan modifications, but also forbearance plans, short sale agreements, and deed-in-lieu of foreclosure programs. Loss mitigation application means any oral or written request for a loss mitigation option that is accompanied by any information required by a servicer for evaluation for a loss mitigation option. Id. Under RESPA, [ s ] ervicer means a person responsible for servicing a federally related mortgage loan ( including the person who makes or holds such loan if such person also services the loan ). Id. Servicing means receiving any scheduled periodic payments from a borrower pursuant to the terms of any federally related mortgage loan, including amounts for escrow accounts... and making the payments to the owner of the loan or other third parties of principal and interest and such other payments with respect to the amounts received from the borrower as XXXX be required pursuant to the terms of the mortgage servicing loan documents or contract. Id. LoanCare is a servicer pursuant to RESPA. CFPB regulations effective XX/XX/XXXX, as well as RESPA itself, require servicers, through amendments made by the Dodd-Frank Act, to take timely action to correct errors relating to avoiding foreclosure, suggesting that borrowers should be able to assert under RESPA errors related to loss mitigation. See 12 U.S.C. 2605 ( k ) ( 1 ) ( C ). Thus, CFPBs new provisions are relevant to this this Notice of Error, and pursuant to these new provisions, we request LoanCare process this Notice of Error as follows : The servicer must acknowledge receipt of a notice of error within five days ( excluding holidays, XXXX, and XXXX ) after receiving the notice, rather than the XXXX business day period under the former law. See Reg. X, 12 C.F.R. 1024.35 ( d ) ( effective Jan. 10, 2014 ). Alternatively, the servicer need not provide this acknowledgment or otherwise satisfy the compliance requirements if it corrects the error or errors asserted by the borrower, and notifies the borrower in writing of the correction, within the five business day period. See Reg. X, 12 C.F.R. 1024.35 ( d ) - ( f ) ( effective Jan. 10, 2014 ) Under RESPA, [ s ] ervicer means a person responsible for servicing a federally related mortgage loan ( including the person who makes or holds such loan if such person also services the loan ). 12 U.S.C. 2605 ( i ). Servicing means receiving any scheduled periodic payments from a borrower pursuant to the terms of any federally related mortgage loan, including amounts for escrow accounts... and making the payments to the owner of the loan or other third parties of principal and interest and such other payments with respect to the amounts received from the borrower as may be required pursuant to the terms of the mortgage servicing loan documents or contract. Id. Based on the representations made to me and the foregoing definitions, it is clear that LoanCare holds itself out as the servicer of my loan and that its activities with respect to the loan meet the definition of servicing. LoanCare is required to respond and correct the above noted errors as it is a standard servicer duty. Under 12 U.S.C. 2605 ( k ) ( 1 ) ( C ) a servicer shall not fail to take timely action to respond to a borrowers requests to correct errors relating to allocation of payments, final balances for purposes of paying off the loan, or avoiding foreclosure, or other standard servicers duties. These errors on LoanCare part must be addressed and reconciled immediately, specifically, pursuant to Regulation X, 12 C.F.R. 1024.35 ( d ) and ( e ), LoanCare has 5 days within which to acknowledge receipt of this request and must respond no later than 7 days. Be advised that RESPA and Regulation X provide a private right of action if a servicer fails to comply with the statute or regulation. 12 U.S.C. 2605 ( f ) ; 12 C.F.R. 1024.41 ( a ). I am a borrower entitled to the protections codified at 12 U.S.C.A. 2605 and 12 C.F.R. 1024.41. The mortgage loan subject to this action is a federally related mortgage as defined in 12 C.F.R.1024.2 and involves a consumer transaction at the time the loan was taken out by me. LoanCare is a mortgage servicer subject to the mandatory requirements of 12 U.S.C.A. 2605 and 12 C.F.R. 1024.41.
