This is a complaint over the application process in my attempt to receive a loan modification or trial forbearance on my current loan with Rushmore Loan Servicing. I have complaints over the delays and miscommunication on Rushmore 's part, but also I have complaints with Rushmore over my attempts to communicate with the company to fix an issue with the application process. This is the second time now over the past several months that Rushmore Loan Servicing and the prior Rushmore servicing department has either delayed my application process for a loan modification or actually outright declined my application. In both instances, the company has claimed that my application was " incomplete '' and therefore could not be reviewed. In both instances, I received assurances orally over the phone by Rushmore representatives that my application package was indeed " complete '' and that Rushmore 's loss mitigation department had all of the documents they needed to review my application package for a loan modification or a trial forbearance. I have filed a previous complaint with the CFPB over Rushmore 's previous servicing department 's actions in my previous attempt last year to receive a loan modification or trial forbearance. This current complaint will focus on Rushmore 's closing of my file on XXXX, thereby nullifying my attempt in my latest effort to receive a loan modification or trial forbearance after claiming that my application was " incomplete '' and that not all documents requested of me were provided. Again, the closing of my file came after I was assured orally by phone on two different occasions by Rushmore representatives that my application was " complete '' and that Rushmore 's loss mitigation department had all of the documents needed to proceed with a review of my application. I have already written Rushmore a letter dated XXXX requesting that they reopen my file and fairly review my application for a loan modification or trial forbearance. I have also made several requests for my single point of contact or a member of Rushmore 's management team to contact me by phone. But as of this date, no one has contacted me. This continues a pattern that I have experienced with Rushmore of absolutely horrendous communication on their part. I will now provide more background on the current situation with my attempt of a loan modification and my application that has been filed. I called Rushmore 's loss mitigation department in early XXXX of XXXX inquiring as to the status of my application for a loan modification or trial forbearance. I was then informed by a Rushmore representative that my file had been " closed '' due to my loan modification application being deemed " incomplete '' by underwriters in Rushmore 's loss mitigation department. I was told that letters had been forwarded to my attorney back in XXXX of this year stating that my modification application was incomplete and that more paystubs were needed. I was also told that a XXXX letter stating that my file had been closed due to an incomplete application had also been forwarded to my attorney. However, this correspondence was never received by either my attorney or myself via email or regular mail through the XXXX postal service. My attorney did forward other Rushmore letters that had been forwarded to us dating back to last year, but again, the above referenced letters were not sent to us and my attorney can verify this fact. I have been in touch with Rushmore 's loss mitigation team periodically by phone over the past few months in phone calls always originated on my part, not Rushmore. On two occasions, I was made aware by Rushmore representatives that one additional paystub was needed to complete my application for a loan modification. The representatives used the term " valuation '' during our first phone conversation and they were confused with what the term meant and actually what was needed to complete the application after I asked them what a valuation document was. It was finally determined that valuation meant forwarding an additional paystub as I stated above. I then immediately forwarded via email a paystub to Rushmore 's loss mitigation department back in XX/XX/year> and then, after being informed orally by phone by a Rushmore representative in XX/XX/year> that a further paystub was needed to complete the loan modification package, I actually provided two additional paystubs, one more than was actually requested. In my early XXXX phone call with a Rushmore representative, I was informed by the representative that the paystubs had not been received, even though I sent the pay information to the email address provided to me by Rushmore 's loss mitigation department. Since that phone call, I have now provided an additional two paystubs to Rushmore in an attempt to have them reopen my file and fairly review my application for a loan modification or trial forbearance. What is extremely troubling with this current situation, as I stated above, is that I was told by two different Rushmore representatives in the loss mitigation department on two different occasions in the early weeks of 2024, that my loan modification application was indeed " complete '' and that all documents I had forwarded to Rushmore were sufficient for an honest review. It obviously then came as quite a shock to me when I was informed earlier this month by Rushmore representatives that another paystub was needed to complete my loan modification application. Once again, I was under the assumption after the earlier telephone communications with Rushmore loss mitigation staff, that my loan modification application was complete and would be therefore be fairly reviewed for a loan modification or trial forbearance. Concluding, I have been informed by Rushmore 's loss mitigation staff in two separate telephone conference calls in early XXXX that my loan modification package was " complete '' and that all documents I had provided were sufficient for an honest review in my attempt to receive a loan modification or trial forbearance. Then, in follow up calls with Rushmore staff, I was then informed by Rushmore staff that my loan modification package was not complete and that more pay information was needed to complete the package. I then emailed additional pay information to Rushmore 's loss mitigation department to an address provided by Rushmore staff. I even provided extra pay documents that were not even requested of me. There is an egregious lack of communication on the part of Rushmore 's loss mitigation department, both in the paucity of the communication and the accuracy of the communication. The department doesn't appear to keep track of documents it receives from borrowers and appears to use delaying tactics under the guise of not having a " complete '' loan modification package in order to not carry out fair reviews of borrowers loan modification applications. Once again, I am deeply troubled by Rushmore 's actions, not only in my situation, but with their dealings with other borrowers as well. In short, Rushmore can't keep track of loan modification documents it receives and also doesn't return phone calls and effectively communicate via mail with borrowers such as myself. It appears that the company uses delaying tactics to not fairly review borrowers applications for loan modifications and trial forbearances.

The Partial Claim is a zero-interest subordinate lien that will include a portion of the amount to be resolved and if you meet the requirements, a principal deferment. Bank of America stated repeatedly in their opposition to complaint in bankruptcy on XX/XX/XXXX by attorney XXXX and later that my loan is a federally backed mortgage and that it was securitized by XXXX. It is settled ( relevant to federally backed mortgages ) that the applicable law is federal. In a decision that has become a leading case on the question, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, arising under the National Housing Act, Title II, 12 U.S.C. 1707 ff. we held : But we do find it to be clear that the source of the law governing the relations between the United States and the parties to the mortgage here involved is federal. ( Citations omitted ) * * * It is therefore equally clear that if the law of the State of Washington is to have any application in the foreclosure proceeding it is not because it applies of its own force, but because either the Congress, the FHA, or the Federal Court adopts the local rule to further federal policy. 268 F.2d at 382. The first question is whether the Congress adopted state law in its definition of mortgage and first mortgage. California argues that it did. The language relied upon appears in 12 U.S.C. 1736 ( a ), and reads : The term mortgage means a first mortgage on real estate, in fee simple. We rejected Californias argument in View Crest, supra, where identical language in 12 U.S.C. 1707 was relied upon. We said : The argument is that in adopting the state definition of first mortgage, Congress intended to adopt all the incidents of the mortgage relation under state law including remedies on default and the appointment of receivers. That this is not the case is clear from reading section 1713 of the same Act which defines certain acts as being in default ( part g ) and sets out certain remedies that the FHA can pursue such as institution of foreclosure ( part k ) proceedings without reference to whether or not there is such a remedy for the default described in the State where the property is located. Moreover, there is no apparent reason for assuming that Congress in incorporating by reference certain duties under state law also meant to restrict the United States to the state remedies for breach of those duties * * 268 F.2d at 382. Therefore, Bank Of America can not foreclose nonjudicially under Alaska law when the mortgage is federally back mortgage. Bank Of America recorded on XX/XX/XXXX a 6th noncompliant notice of default and sale for XX/XX/XXXX in blatant disregard to Congress and the federal courts that clearly determined that federally backed mortgages are under federal and not under state law unless Congress specifically adopted Alaska nonjudicial law, which Congress never did. All while knowing that this default is time-barred since XXXX as determined in the bankruptcy court denial of Bank Of America motion to dismiss my complaint on the sole ground that Bank of America was already time-barred in order dated XX/XX/XXXX.

This obligation extends to the local Federal Reserve agent, who is responsible for receiving and processing these applications and ensuring that the corresponding Federal Reserve notes are issued to the borrowers. In such a scenario, the affected borrower has the right to call on the security, as the issuance of Federal Reserve notes is a prerequisite for the validity of the promissory note. Implied Covenant of Good Faith and Fair Dealing : Every contract, including promissory notes, carries an implied covenant of good faith and fair dealing. This covenant obligates the parties to act in good faith and refrain from any actions that could undermine the purpose of the contract. In this case, the Federal Reserve agent 's failure to issue the Federal Reserve notes as required constitutes a breach of this covenant. 4. Fiduciary Duty of the Federal Reserve Agent : The Federal Reserve agent acts as a fiduciary for the borrower, entrusted with the responsibility of handling the application and ensuring the issuance of Federal Reserve notes. Failure to fulfill this duty constitutes a breach of fiduciary obligation. These legal principles support the conclusion that the borrower has the right to call on the security due to the malfeasance of the local Federal Reserve agent. When we purchased our home in XX/XX/XXXX, we took out a loan from XXXXXXXX XXXX a.k.a. XXXX XXXX. We also purchased homeowners insurance from XXXX. The insurance policy was renewed in XXXX, with the premium being paid out of escrow. It was renewed again in XXXX, also, with the payment being made from escrow. In XX/XX/XXXX, Chase took over as the mortgagor after acquiring the mortgage from XXXX XXXX. At that time, Chase received all the information concerning the mortgage, including information about the homeowners insurance policy from XXXX, which again, had been renewed with a payment from escrow for two consecutive years without fail. Despite this, when it came time to pay the renewal premium for the insurance, Chase did not pay it, and they allowed the policy to lapse. In early XX/XX/XXXX, I received a letter from Chase informing me that Chase did not have proof of active homeowners insurance. I contacted XXXX and received a copy of my policy, which I uploaded to Chase 's website, as instructed in the letter. At that time, I was informed by XXXX that the payment for the premium needed to be made through escrow. In fact, there was no option to pay the premium myself on the XXXX website or app at all. The payment must come from Chase through escrow, as it had in XX/XX/XXXX and XX/XX/XXXX. After uploading my insurance paperwork to Chase 's website, I received another letter from Chase, indicating that they did not have proof of active insurance for the home. The letter threatened that if I did not promptly upload proof of active homeowners insurance, Chase would purchase insurance on my behalf at a higher cost and with lower coverage than what I could purchase on the open market. Again, I contacted the insurance company, and they told me that the payment needed to come from escrowi.e., Chase . At that point, I am running in circles between Chase and XXXX and facing threats that Chase will take actions to my financial detriment. To avoid an unreasonable charge for deficient insurance, I purchased new insurance from XXXX ( XXXX ) and uploaded the information to Chase 's website. A few weeks later, I received an email from Chase indicating that they had paid the insurance premium for my new XXXX ( XXXX ) policy out of escrow. In other words, after I provided proof that I had purchased and paid for a new insurance policy based on threats from Chase about buying insurance on my behalf, Chase made a duplicate payment for the premium. Accordingly, I contacted Chase to find out : ( a ) how to get a refund for the duplicate payment of the premium; and ( b ) why Chase did not pay the premium to XXXX through escrow in the first place, which again, had occurred in two consecutive years without incident. My call with Chase was incredibly frustrating to say the least. We got into a long discussion about a technical issue with the policy where they were claiming they could not pay the premium because they did not have a " renewal declaration for the insurance policy. Rather than contacting the insurer to get the requisite information, they allowed the policy to lapse, and then, claimed they couldn't pay for the policy because it had expired. Lets pause here, as there are XXXXhree points I want to make sure are clear. First, we did not request to have our mortgage transferred from XXXX to Chase. Chase chose to take over the mortgage and informed us that it would be our mortgage handler as of XX/XX/XXXX. Chase requires proof of insurance for its mortgages. When it allowed our policy to lapse, I received a letter the very next day. In our recent conversation, their insurance team confirmed that they did indeed receive the information about our insurance in XX/XX/XXXX. Simply put, they had the information they needed to maintain our insurance and failed to do so. Second, our insurance carrier was baffled when I attempted to pay for the premium directly. According to the carrier, the payment should come from escrow, which is why they did not even have a payment mechanism on their website or app to pay the premium directly. Third, Chase never contacted us to work with us on getting whatever they claim they need to renew the policy for a third consecutive year. Rather, they sent a letter threatening to buy expensive deficient insurance on our behalf unless we uploaded proof of an active policy. As a financial institution working directly with consumers, Chase could have made a minimum amount of effort to keep our policy active. They also could have contacted our insurer to get that information, as again, they had all the policy documents when they took over the mortgage in XX/XX/XXXX. Instead, they chose to send us a form letter with confusing and ambiguous threats. Chase 's actions were irresponsible, and their attempts to shirk responsibility now and blame us for their failure to pay premium out of escrow is shameful. It's hard to understand what exactly their endgame is with this oversight and lack of accountability, but it has shaken our confidence in the company. By failing to pay the premium and allowing our policy to lapse, Chase potentially put us at significant financial risk, and their bad faith behavior evidences an established practice and procedure of failing to perform mortgage obligations and attempting to shift blame onto their customers, who are ordinary consumers.

CMG Financial is the company that provided me Mortgage for my house. I recently called them to request them how I could make bi-weekly payments to pay-off my mortgage sooner. I tried performing this payment change on my account over the internet, but their platform does not allow me to schedule this type of payments. During the call, they told me that in order to enroll in the bi-weekly auto drafting program, I had to request that over the phone, they'd send me a letter, and I'd have to fill out a form and send it back to them. The letter took more than 15 days to arrive, and they have a cut-off day of the month if you want to have the bi-weekly payments to arrive on the following month. In order to make that happen, I had to rush it by sending a FAX of the form. After a few days, they replied saying that they could not start the auto-drafting because I did not pay the next month ahead. This is not something they disclosed beforehand, and it feels like they keep putting obstacles for people who want to pay-off sooner or reduce their interest burden. I had issues, for example, with making payments to my principal. You can't make payments towards the principal at any point during the month. There is a window, and if you're not in this window, they won't take your money. Luckily, I had made a payment towards my principal this month that was larger than my monthly dues, and I questioned them why I wasn't considered to be ahead on my mortgage for the bi-weekly autodrafting to begin. The representative said that it was " only '' a payment towards the principal, and in order to be considered ahead, I'd have to pay principal, interest, and escrow ahead, then I would have to also issue the bi-weekly payments for the same month that I just paid. Moreover, they said that the only benefit of bi-weekly payments was that you issued only XXXX extra payment per year, and no interest benefits come out of it. Reducing the interest burden is the sole purpose of paying bi-weekly. The way that CMG Financial works on this is by holding what is considered the first payment of the month without putting that towards your account and continues to charge you interest over that amount until the second payment of the month is issued. When that payment comes in, it is combined with the first, and applied to the account, and at that point the interest rate over the principal paid for the month stops accruing. Not only this business is creating undue burdens for people to pay-off their mortgage sooner, they're holding your money and illegally charging interest over money you paid towards the mortgage and that they have on hand. Neither the contract, nor the forms I used to file, mention these constraints. I have never found any other respectable financial institution that would cause so much trouble for people trying to be responsible and pay-off their mortgages. CFPB needs to step in, and force the business to change these policies and make it easier for people to make responsible financial decisions instead of putting roadblocks that discourages them from paying off early, plus, charging interest over money that I already paid and which they received is illegal, and they must immediately stop this practice.

text: I am the owner and occupant of a single-family home that I have sought repeated assistance from Rushmore Servicing to avoid foreclosure. He asked for access to the one car garage whereby the access door is broken and there is no entry point from inside the house. I was unable to help him get inside the garage. We gave him permission to go inside however he could, but he determined he couldnt get inside. The next thing we heard was that we had blocked the appraiser from accessing the one car garage to do his measurements. The real estate company called him to come back over to the property and said they would send people to help him get inside but he refused to return. Rushmore Servicing also refused to release any of the two internal valuations to myself or my representatives although they added the cost to my statements. Several purchase offers were sent to Rushmore that they denied for unknown reason and never revealed what the value of the property was by their own inspectors. My home needs serious repairs. I was told they wanted to do a 3rd inspection. I agreed. They never sent anyone. Then I was told that my loss mitigation application was cancelled on XX/XX/XXXX and Rushmore offered no reason why and never sent a denial letter. I diligently complied with all document requests during the entire loss mitigation procedure and waited patiently for Rushmore Servicings review. My application was canceled for no reason and after two inspections Rushmore refused to tell me what the property value was so I could seek to find a buyer to pay that price. As months went by, Rushmore became increasingly less communicative. They locked my account access online and I could no longer view letters or my statements. Rushmores loss mitigation department denied any further remedies in settling the mortgage debt, which is a violation against my rights under Loss Mitigation Procedures 12 C.F.R. 1024.41. They just canceled everything after I waited for months. Rushmore Service acted in a disingenuous fashion in an attempt to disenfranchise me during my settlement. Second, Rushmore was required to review additional loss mitigation options before proceeding with foreclosure. This was all a continuing attempt to deny my rights in regards to settling the outstanding debts owed and violating my rights as I try to not go through a foreclosure.

In XXXX of XXXX, our property suffered devastating water damage due to frozen pipes. Working in partnership with our insurance company, a mitigation contractor and his team spent weeks filling multiple dumpsters with nearly every interior piece of our 113-year-old beloved XXXX two-flat. When the insurance company issued the {$67000.00} check to reimburse our contractor for his work, I was startled to see that the check was made out to our mortgage company as well. Our contractor reassured us that most companies are able to turn around their endorsement in a day or two. I opened a claim with them, found out what information they needed, gathered it, and overnighted them the endorsed check. They told me it would take 8 to 10 business days. I waited. Once that time had elapsed, I followed up, and found that instead of getting my money to pay my lovely, hardworking contractor, I was getting tortured in the absolute deepest depth of greedy bureaucratic XXXX. To be clear, the work is done. They do not need to inspect any repairs ; it's mitigation work only. They have photos, they have invoices, they have the assessors report. They have everything they asked for. They continue to hold my money, presumably profiting off the interest, while taking no discernable action toward disbursing it back to me. Every day, I ask what has been done to address my claim and disburse these funds. Every day, I am told that the thing that I was told the day prior will perhaps now maybe be done today. Some days, they ask me to do something, like take a photo of a street sign. Some days, they say they might give me some of my money. Some days, they say they want to schedule an inspection. Do they schedule the inspection? No, somebody requests that somebody else request that it be scheduled, but nobody ever actually does it. This is, bar none, the worst experience I have ever had with any business of any sort. It is greedy. It is incompetent. It is unconscionable. Did you read XXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX? It's like that, but more absurd. It's frankly more tragic, because the small business owner who did tens and tens of thousands of dollars of backbreaking labor in order to help us save our home? He's the one waiting for something that nobody can assure me is coming.

More concerning is the many, massive cracks that have appeared in the walls, ceiling, over doorways & windows. There is also noticeable water intrusion that is occurring all over the home, through the ceiling & also through cracks in the wall. No room is spared, the are cracks & water intrusion in every part of the home. This was not pointed out in the inspection. I contacted a foundation company & was advised the foundation is damaged. There has been significant foundation movement since the inspection until now ( approx 7 months ). There is a seam going from the ceiling to the floor where the addition to the house was built. The arch in the transition where the back of the house used to be going to the addition is sagging & has significant cracks. The foundation tech advised the the old back of the home is collapsing inward & the addition is sinking outward so there is a disconnection taking place. Also, the side of the home where the bedrooms are located is sinking, The estimated repair costs are $ XXXX $ XXXX I called a roofing company to determine the cause of the water intrusion & why the ceiling are cracking & falling in. I discovered that water leaks out the back of the home when the shower is running. The lower back of the home is saturated with water & the siding is coming off. I do not have an estimate for this yet. The drywall in the home is so compromised that the brand new cabinets that were installed by the seller are now pulling away from the wall. The curtains I hung are constantly falling because the screws can not be secured in the damaged walls. The seller installed new ceiling fans & light fixtures & there are cracks radiating from the holes where the fixtures were installed in each room. This is a safety issue. There is water intrusion around an electrical outlet in the XXXX bedroom, which is also a safety issue. I also discovered two areas on the back of the home where there is no wood or siding. There is just a big piece of thin sheet metal covering the hole in house. One is located by the kitchen plumbing, which explains why the pipes froze when the temperature dipped during the winter. The other spot is where the utilities connect to the home. I have not had a chance to investigate this issue. The AC/Heating does not work in the XXXX bedroom & in the addition to the home. I have not gotten an estimate for this issue. Twelve of thirteen windows need to be replaced. The inspection pointed out two. The estimate for this is $ XXXX From just what I know there is at least $ XXXX worth of repairs, but clearly I have not scratched the surface in finding the issues with this home. My issue is I purchased this home through a series of referrals. NAF referred to XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX referred me to the inspector XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX. Somehow, through all these referrals I wound up paying full market value for a home that essentially needs to be rebuilt from the ground up & has issues with every major system. Re : Formal Complaint Against Ameris Bank for Violating Truth in Lending Act ( TILA ) and Predatory Lending Practices Dear Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, We are writing to file a formal complaint against Ameris Bank for engaging in predatory lending practices that violate the Truth in Lending Act ( TILA ) pursuant to 15 U.S.C. Chapter 41, Consumer Credit Protection. We believe that our experience with Ameris Bank constitutes a clear breach of consumer protection laws and warrants investigation and action. We obtained a one-time close construction-to-permanent 31-year loan from Ameris Bank for the construction of our new home . The terms of the loan were explained to me by my loan officer who assured me that my 4 % interest rate would be locked, and we would have the option to modify to a lower rate after construction or keep my initial construction phase rate. We closed on the loan on XX/XX/2021, with the understanding that we would make interest-only payments for the first 12-months, followed by full mortgage payments thereafter. However, despite being current on my mortgage payments and following the terms outlined in my mortgage documents, Ameris Bank forced us to refinance the loan to avoid foreclosure. The bank claimed default due to delays in construction caused by factors beyond our control, such as labor and supply shortages exacerbated by the COVID-19 pandemic. This forced refinance resulted in significant financial loss for us, as we were forced to accept a much higher interest rate of 7.5 % with another lender and pay closing fees. Furthermore, Ameris Bank failed to disclose essential information about the risks associated with construction loans, including potential delays and the possibility of additional fees for extensions. Other banks, such as XXXX XXXX, offered free extensions for construction-permanent loans, while Ameris Bank XXXX XXXX impose egregious fees ( .5 % of loan amount per month ) for a 6-month extension followed by a full refinance for 30-year mortgage portion to a market rate, paying closing costs, essentially, treating it as a 2-time closing loan. Despite our builder 's pleas and our attorney 's attempts to resolve the situation and provide evidence of our compliance with the loan terms, our consistent payment history of full mortgage payments as agreed to in the mortgage note, Ameris Bank proceeded with threatening foreclosure, disregarding the fact that we were ahead on payments according to our mortgage documents and amortization schedule. Moreover, Ameris Bank made misleading statements regarding the terms of our loan, including falsely claiming that our interest rate was no longer locked and attempting to impose penalties and fees not specified in the loan agreement. We believe that Ameris Bank 's actions constitute predatory lending practices and violate the Truth in Lending Act, which aims to protect consumers from unfair and deceptive lending practices. We respectfully request that Consumer Financial Protection Bureau investigate this matter and take appropriate action to hold Ameris Bank accountable for its actions. Enclosed with this letter are copies of relevant documents, including loan agreements, correspondence with the bank, and communication with our attorney, to support our complaint. Thank you for your attention to this matter. We look forward to a prompt resolution and justice for us and other consumers whove suffered financially due to illegal tactics by Ameris Bank. We request compensation for escalated cost of the loan from 4 % to 7.5 % over 30-year term, our attorney fees, and closing costs.

First we had a payment modification, it lowered the payment to {$50.00} which I made those payments. Then we entered in to a forbearance. that stated if i make XXXX consecutive payments of {$1100.00} we would do a loan Modification. I completed that and the loan modification was done. I went to check my credit report and it showed that I was 180 days late. This is a violation of the CARES act. Mortgage Forbearance : The CARES Act provided relief for homeowners facing financial hardship due to the pandemic by allowing them to request forbearance on their federally backed mortgages. Forbearance allowed borrowers to temporarily pause or reduce their mortgage payments for a specified period, typically up to 180 days, with the possibility of extension. Credit Reporting during Forbearance : Under the CARES Act, if a borrower entered into a forbearance agreement with their mortgage servicer, the servicer was required to report the loan status to credit bureaus as " current '' if the borrower was current on their payments before entering forbearance. This provision aimed to prevent borrowers from being penalized on their credit reports solely due to the pandemic-related financial hardship. No Negative Impact on Credit Scores : Borrowers who received mortgage forbearance under the CARES Act were generally protected from negative impacts on their credit scores. Credit reporting agencies were instructed to ensure that mortgage forbearance did not adversely affect borrowers ' credit scores or creditworthiness. Communications with Creditors : The CARES Act also required mortgage servicers to work with borrowers to provide accurate information about their forbearance status and ensure that borrowers understood their options for mortgage relief. This included providing clear and timely communications about the terms of forbearance, any changes to mortgage payments, and the impact on credit reporting.

This is the appeal letter I sent to PHH mortgage that describes exactly what happened : To whom it may concern, I wanted to go ahead and appeal the decision to not remove my PMI that was informed to me on XX/XX/XXXX. To begin, I wanted to describe the story and experience from my end. I requested to have my PMI removed and received a letter dated on XX/XX/XXXX ( Please see the attached letter provided to me ). This letter described the exact process of how to get the PMI removed and what the eligibility requirements were. The letter stated one option for PMI removal was to request a property valuation to verify the current market value of my house to be at least {$740000.00}. The letter also noted that if XXXX years had not elapsed since the origination date of the account, that PMI could still removed if substantial improvements were made to the home and the market value had increased as stated above. I was told to include a {$190.00} check within 30 days. The letter specifically states, Note : If the required details are not received within the 30-days, the PMI removal process must be reviewed again to determine the eligibility. I proceeded to call PHH customer service to make sure I knew exactly what needed to be done to remove the PMI and did have some questions about the mention of substantial improvements since at the time it had not been XXXX years. The mortgage originated on XX/XX/XXXX which means XXXX years would have elapsed on XX/XX/XXXX. I was told by a member from your customer service team that I could send the check within 30 days and send the list of substantial improvements ; or wait until XX/XX/XXXX after XXXX years have elapsed and send a check before the 30 day period elapsed. In order to avoid confusion, I did just that and sent the check through priority mail and made sure it arrived before the 30-day period ended. My bank statement shows that the check was cashed on XX/XX/XXXX. However, my tracking confirmation shows that the check arrived to your department before XX/XX/XXXX ( the 30 day period end date ). I did not have to send the check so close to the end of the 30-day period, but again was explicitly told by one of your customer service members to wait until after my XXXX year origination date of my mortgage. If I knew what I know now, I would have sent in a check immediately to get the process started earlier and sent in the substantial home improvements we have done to our house. I was told that each conversation with customer service is recorded, so I would appreciate if you could retrieve this recording to listen to the false information that was given to me. Regardless, of the XXXXyear mark, I will repeat the that the letter states in writing the following : Note : If the required details are not received within the 30-days, the PMI removal process must be reviewed again to determine the eligibility. I have abided by those exact standards and everything was given within 30 days so the original letter requirements should hold true. I proceeded to schedule the BPO appraisal. On a letter dated XX/XX/XXXX ( please see the attached letter provided ), I was told that I was denied the PMI removal. I called the customer service department, where they told me that the BPO appraisal came in at {$750000.00}. This is higher than the {$740000.00} threshold provided to me in writing in the original letter. I was confused and even the customer service member I was talking with was confused as to why the PMI was not being removed. Please see this recording as well. I have then made multiple calls with customer service where my case was assigned to an escalation team. Ultimately, on XX/XX/XXXX I was sent an email that stated that on XX/XX/XXXX the XXXX year mark had passed since my origination date and therefore the LTV threshold went from XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX. I was denied because that would make the appraisal value of {$740000.00} no longer a valid eligibility requirement and the new required value would be much higher than even the {$750000.00} my BPO appraisal came in at. I was told multiple times that this change in LTV is due to investor requirements. The part that I dont understand from all of this is that if this is an investor requirement, why was this not stated on my original PMI removal letter anywhere? Why did the letter not state that I had until XX/XX/XXXX to complete these requirements because after the eligibility will change due to hitting the XXXX year mark on my mortgage? All the letter states is that I had 30 days to comply which I did. Again, I was specifically told by one of your customer service members that even after the XXXX year mark the same requirements would apply as long as everything was received in the 30 day period, which it was. Why was I given false information by your customer service team and by your letters in writing? If all these rules were already known, did I not deserve to be presented the proper information and not flat out lied to? I think this whole process has been completely unacceptable and unprofessional. I have a wife and XXXX XXXX kids that I live with. I am the sole provider of my family. Removing the PMI monthly payment, would mean so much to my family and help me support them further. I am so saddened that due to misinformation I may have to wait XXXX more years ( approximately $ XXXX of more PMI payments to be made ) to have this PMI monthly payment removed. Can you please help me to get this PMI removed? I have followed all the steps and requirements and was clearly misled. If you can not, I will be forced to take other measures and could use litigation or go through the Consumer Finance Protection Bureau for assistance. Thank you for your consideration and I appreciate any help you can provide.

Mr. Cooper Group materially altered the complainants mortgage chattels by applying their own indorsements without her consent. 3. Once Planet Home Lending noticed they didn't have enough money to cover everything, they performed an Escrow Analysis outlining the shortage. Once again, I had no notification that this was happening from their end. The analysis concluded that I had a shortage on my account, and that I must now pay to make up that shortage by adding {$470.00} to my monthly payment. Therefore, I had to do the work to find that documentation that the lender should have already received from the lender they purchased my loan from. On top of that, since they didnt have this information, they allowed the flood insurance already in place to lapse, causing the need for a new quote, and yearly premium. They had already put in place their own expensive flood insurance once again on my behalf without my knowledge or consent. After finally obtaining all this information for them, I emailed the documentation to the supervisor helping me, who then stated it would take 15 days for a refund to be issued to my escrow account. Also, the amount that the new analysis gives for the property taxes paid, does not match the original analysis for the same payment. So, the numbers are not matching up, and seem to be manipulated. Furthermore, the refund that was applied to my account was {$1900.00}, which is significantly lower that the amount that was taken from my account from XXXX to XXXX. Also, once the flood insurance lapsed in XXXX of XXXX, they continued to charge me for their expensive flood insurance every month up until XXXX when they finally renewed the insurance with the proper company for which I provided the quote. I understand that my Home Insurance did rise, but if my escrow account hadnt been improperly handled, I do not feel any shortage should still fall on myself as the consumer. It should be the lenders responsibility to ensure the money I am paying every month is used properly. Otherwise, a compounding affect will take place given my escrow balance will turn negative as shown in the print-out provided. Overall, the fact that this issue and remediation thereof was placed upon the consumer when the issue was clearly caused by the lack of due diligence on the part of the purchasing party when the loan changed hands, is unacceptable, and the hurt that it has caused to myself and my family both emotionally and financially can not not be understated. It is imperative that these types of issues should not be placed on the consumer, especially when it was due to a lack of due diligence on the companys part. Furthermore, something as important as insurance for the consumers home and livelihood should be held with more regard. If there is obviously an issue with something so important, more should be done to contact the consumer ( I was told that a piece of mail was sent through snail mail which I never received ; no phone call, no email, no voicemail ), and never should insurance be purchased on behalf of the consumer without consent, especially knowing that it would cost them XXXX times more a year than what they had been paying. On top of that, a representative for Planet Home Lending customer service state they chose their own in-house flood insurance as coverage, which is obviously a conflict of interest, and are essentially paying themselves. I will add that it is required to have flood insurance, so the company knew I had to of had coverage with the prior lender. It is imperative this issue be resolved, and that consumers in the future do not go through what we have gone through to try and resolve this on the companys behalf.

Subject : Complaint Against Gregory Funding for Mismanagement of HAF Grant Payments and Poor Customer Service Dear Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, My name is XXXX XXXX, and I am writing to file a formal complaint against Gregory Funding concerning their mismanagement of funds provided by the Hardest Hit Fund ( HAF ) and their unacceptable customer service. I received a grant from the HAF designed to help homeowners stay current on their mortgage payments and prevent foreclosure. This grant made 18 payments of approximately {$990.00} each to Gregory Funding, with my monthly mortgage payment being about {$910.00}. Over the past three months, I have repeatedly contacted Gregory Funding regarding discrepancies in my account. Despite the grant payments, I have noticed a monthly credit of around {$1200.00}, and I am unclear about how these payments have been applied. I have encountered the following issues : Lack of Transparency and Misapplication of Funds : Gregory Funding representatives have informed me that the grant money was applied to my account. However, the HAF fund manager explained that the funds should only be used for monthly payments and any remaining credit should be applied to the next month 's payment. Instead, it appears that Gregory Funding has applied these funds to the principal without my permission or notification. The credit amount left over should have been applied to the payments for XXXX and partially for XX/XX/year>, as there should be a remaining credit. Inability to Access Account : For several months, I have been unable to log in to my account to make payments. Despite multiple calls to Gregory Funding for assistance, this issue remains unresolved. Unprofessional and Rude Customer Service : Almost every agent I have spoken with has been unhelpful and rude. I requested to speak with a supervisor to file a complaint and seek an explanation, but I have received no response. These issues have caused significant stress and confusion, and I believe they reflect a serious mismanagement of my mortgage account by Gregory Funding. A fair resolution to this issue would be : Application of Remaining Credit : The remaining credit should be applied to the monthly payments, not the principal, as initially agreed upon by the HAF grant. Detailed Explanation and Account Reconciliation : A detailed explanation of how my grant payments have been applied, including a reconciliation of my account showing the application of each HAF grant payment. Restoration of Account Access : Restoration of my ability to access my account online. Investigation of Customer Service Practices : An investigation into the customer service practices at Gregory Funding. I would appreciate your assistance in resolving these issues. Please let me know if you require any additional information or documentation. Thank you for your attention to this matter. Sincerely, XXXX XXXX

They paid without my knowledge, without my approval and without necessity - and also without checking to see whether the false information they received was legitimate. On two occasions in XXXX my condo lawyer lied to them and they quickly paid her, without my knowledge, approval or necessity and in violation of my rights. Both caused me irreparable harm. The first case led to the cancellation of a temporary restraining order TRO hearing scheduled before a judge on XX/XX/XXXX, to challenge false accusations and charges to prevent an auction sale of my condo unless I paid {$26000.00} by XX/XX/XXXX. My lawyer and I were prepared to challenge the charges. I might have owed some late fees. Two hours before the TRO, my lawyer told me the TRO was cancelled because my XXXX lawyer got Chase to pay her off the same day. According to her time records she spent 6 hours preparing for the TRO but got Chase to collude with her on cancelling my TRO when she realized that she would lose in the hearing. This was an obstruction of justice and sabotaged my right to due process. I was very upset with Chase and spoke to them and wrote to them. I later found out that they actually overpaid my XXXX lawyer {$37000.00} based on an earlier claim that was dismissed because of errors. Chase should not have paid. Because of this I owe that money to Chase and since I was denied justice I had to declare bankruptcy which caused me damages. In the second case my condo lawyer lied to Chase and told them I was not paying my condo fees. I was. it led to false accusations, defamation and retaliation from my condo XXXX, telling me I was not in good standing and not letting me vote. The XXXX president told me that the condo lawyer told him that I was not paying my condo fees and that my mortgage company was paying them. After hours of investigation I found out that Chase had been paying my condo fees for 15 months, as was I. The management company received 2 checks a month - one from me and one from Chase. I asked them to stop paying. I had to put it in wiring to get them to stop. Every time I spoke to staff at Chase they mindlessly repeated that they were protecting their interests. Nothing they did actually protected their interests but violated mine. They told me that I agreed to that in our contract. I did not agree to them automatically paying money based on lies, colluding with fraud, without informing me. The contract Chase kept telling me I agreed to is an " adhesion contract '' " where the parties are of such disproportionate bargaining power that the party of weaker bargaining power could not have negotiated for variations in the terms of the contract '' with " terms to be especially egregious to standards of fair play. '' This contract should be considered unconscionable and void on the grounds of evidence of procedural unconscionability include duress, fraud, undue influence, and fine print. After having been violated twice I spoke often with Chase staff and suggested they change their policy to simply inform people and get their approval before paying money. Chase also told me they never investigate- they just pay instantly with no scrutiny. On several occasions on the phone and in writing, I told XXXX that there would never be any occasion that they would ever have to pay a penny on my behalf and demanded that they inform me and get my approval first. They refused. I told them I had a XXXX XXXX due to exposure to toxic mold in my condo. I have problems with XXXX function - trouble with reading, writing, organizing and dealing with desk work, mail and paperwork. I also have XXXX XXXX and brain fog. I told them I needed to be informed by phone, primarily and secondarily by email. They refused for years and said they don't do that. I said according to the XXXX XXXX XXXX they are required to accommodate my XXXX. I said it was easier to make a phone call than to go though all of this. Eventually someone on the phone said they would and some said they wouldn't. Then some time in XXXX, I think, I had a new problem with Chase. I found out that Chase paid my DC Property Taxes around XX/XX/XXXX and twice after. I had no idea. With my neurological XXXX somethings things fall through the cracks. I missed XXXX property tax payment. Had Chase called me to accommodate my XXXX as repeatedly requested on the phone and in wiring, I would have instantly walked across the street to the bank and paid my property taxes like I usually do. I had no idea Chase would pay. I did pay the next two, but Chase kept paying my property taxes, even when I was also paying, without my knowledge, approval or necessity. I got a letter from DC tax office that I had a credit. Note that all of these instances caused me a lot of stress, disrupted my work and wasted hours and hours and hours of my time on the phone and writing emails and trying to correct and resolve an absurd situation. I told Chase again that they failed to accommodate my XXXX. Again, they repeated their mantra that they were protecting their interests. I called Chase and tried to put a stop to this disruptive ongoing arrangement to resolve it once and for all. They said I could do an investigation with their XXXX XXXX. I was delighted and naively imagined they would investigate their collusion with fraud and would then accommodate my XXXX and never ever pay money again without my approval. We went through an illusory process but nothing changed. I don't exactly understand this because of my neurological issues, but they raised my monthly mortgage amount with an escrow account. I have my mortgage on automatic Billpay and have never missed a payment. I have been told I was behind several payments and owe thousands of dollars. Since XXXX, XXXX, Chase has refused to accept my payments. I refuse to pay the higher amount caused by their refusal to accommodate my XXXX. I think this might be extortion. I am now threatened with foreclosure for charges incurred by their violations of my rights. I had no idea about this until I got an email from my former bankruptcy lawyer in XXXX. They contacted him. I didn't know I got a letter from Chase, sent to my condo that I moved out of. I started receiving CDs in the mail, almost daily from Chase which I played in my car which was a recitation of numbers I didn't understand. Then Chase sent me what I imagine is a copy of my statement in XXXX, which I don't read. Chase was bizarrely accommodating XXXX that I don't have, which require far more work and expense to burn CDs or print out XXXX and put in the mail, than to make a simple phone call. Once again, I have another investigation with Chase 's XXXX XXXX hoping to resolve this. I said I was willing to pay the amount of my mortgage payments that I legitimately owe but refuse their illegitimate increase. Over the years I have had numerous contacts with Chase by phone and email. Many of the staff seem to be understanding and gave me the illusion of willingness to address these issues in good faith and resolve them once and for all. They have all failed 100 % so far. They are like automatons and still repeat they are protecting their interests and I agreed to a contract and nothing changes. Many have said they won't call me for approval I contacted the XXXX XXXX firm handling my foreclosure and they have been responsive and contacted Chase for escalation of the investigation, which is pending. I am worried. My expectations are low. I hope the CFPB can help. There has to be a law preventing them from doing this.

When we reached question 4, I requested a three-month extension to our forbearance plan. However, I did not state that we could repay the forbearance plan. I simply answered " no '' when asked if our situation had changed, referencing our new, unexpected {$1000.00} monthly HOA bill that we were navigating. My account has not been properly labeled or documented. Nearing the end of our three-month forbearance program from XX/XX/2024, I requested an extension, not a statement of refusal to their four exit questions. The following day, I called Wells Fargo to express my concerns about the unclear information provided by the call representative and to seek further assistance regarding our situation. Throughout my communications, I consistently expressed our desire to begin repaying so as not to appear delinquent and sought clarity on the required monthly payments. I submitted payments at the beginning and end of XXXX. Despite this, there have been multiple errors and discrepancies in Wells Fargo 's handling of my case. For example, a letter requiring a response within 20 days arrived eight or nine days late, which is unfair to mortgage consumers. Additionally, when I inquired about unclear documents, including one indicating my file was incomplete, I was told by an agent that these packets were automated and not to worry. The most concerning issue is that the case escalation manager handling my account did not listen to the correct phone calls for review. On the day I am submitting this complaint, he provided inaccurate information about the phone calls in question. He stated : - **XX/XX/2024 : ** The call lasted 3 minutes and 15 seconds. My phone records, however, show it lasted 6 minutes. - **XX/XX/2024 : ** The call lasted 14 minutes and 22 seconds. My records reflect a 9-minute duration. These discrepancies highlight poor handling and miscommunication. On XX/XX/2024, I informed the escalation manager that the information provided on XXXX XXXX was neither clear nor thorough. He acknowledged that he might not have reviewed the correct call. I was told that Wells Fargo would reconsider the forbearance if there were a change in circumstances. Our situation is not due to a lack of income but an unexpected increase in our monthly HOA fees to {$1000.00}. My file has not been accurately documented regarding our situation. The incorrect logging of call times and the mishandling of our requests are alarming. The two separate phone conversations the escalation manager referenced are not accurate. This mishandling has unfairly moved our mortgage out of forbearance protection and into delinquency. I have further documentation to present, including proof of mortgage payments made this month. The decision regarding my forbearance request handling contains significant inaccuracies, and I have evidence to support this claim. Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.

My mortgage company, Leader One Financial Corporation, fraudulently created a " second mortgage carried piggyback '', when they disclosed through paperwork that they were executing a deferment agreement. This stemmed from a XXXX XXXX related forbearance on my mortgage payments over a 3 month period. The outstanding balance was {$6000.00} that needed to be resolved at the end of the forbearance period. I decided on a deferment agreement, that places this balance at the end of my loan to be paid off when I refinance or pay the house off. Several months ago when I went to access the equity in my home by way of a HELOC, I was told I could not be approved ( although I have approx $ XXXX in equity ) because there is a second " lien '' on my home. For the last several months, I have been making phone calls to the Mortgage Company AND the servicing company " XXXX '' to find the paperwork that allowed them to do this, and what can be done to resolve the issue. To say I have got the " run around '' is a massive understatement. The servicing company has only told me that I CAN NOT pay off the " piggyback loan '', but doesn't have any other information. When I contacted the mortgage company directly, I was able to speak with a live person 1 time, who informed me she would request the " paperwork '' from the servicing company and call me back. I never received a call back, even after subsequent calls and messages left on her voicemail. After a lot of back and forth, I obtained an email address for the servicing company and sent them a formal request on XX/XX/XXXX for the " second piggyback mortgage '' paperwork ( there is none, which is the point ), as well as clarification of whom the money is actually owed to, as this was a Covid related forbearance and deferment agreement. On XX/XX/XXXX I received two letters in the mail dated XX/XX/XXXX. One letter stated that they received my email request and are " researching it ''. The other letter stated that Leader One is transferring my loan to a different servicing provider on XX/XX/XXXX. Obviously the issue isn't going to be answered OR resolved if they are transferring my loan to a different service provider in 3 days. This is a tactic on leader one 's part to absolve themselves of responsibility for the fraudulent creation of a second mortgage.

My husband and I have owned a condominium unit in XXXX XXXX, NC since XXXX. Our unit is covered by a XXXX XXXX policy, which includes, among other things, commercial coverage and flood insurance. This XXXX XXXX policy is renewed every XXXX. Our unit has a mortgage held by Truist Bank. Each year, the bank requires proof of flood insurance coverage. Each year we provide proof that the coverage has been renewed by uploading the new policy onto XXXX website. Each year, Truist replies that it is unable to proceed with updating the policy information and makes a vague statement about whether the date of the submitted documents are current. The policy submitted is always the current, renewed policy. Truist never supplies any list of what is missing in our submission, probably because nothing is missing. The policies submitted have always been renewed and current, showing coverage for the year, as requested by Truist. Each year since XXXX, we have had to go back and forth with Truist submitting the same documents showing current coverage until finally, after months of aggravation, stress and unnecessary wrangling, Truist accepts that the submitted documents do indeed prove current coverage. Although Truist provides a phone number for insurance questions, there is no option to speak with a living human being, and none of the other options is relevant. At least once, in XXXX, Truist tried to force us to pay for an insurance policy that it imposed on us, despite the fact that we already had and had provided proof of adequate flood insurance coverage. Last year I filed a complaint concerning this charade and, due to the CFPBs intervention, Truist accepted the insurance documents we uploaded without the usual dragged-out drama. I am hoping for the same result this year. I can not fathom why Truist engages in this parody each year, but I suspect it must have something to do with the banks hope that it can foist off expensive insurance policies on at least some of its customers. At any rate, I have attached the two insurance documents provided by our insurance agent and uploaded to Truist 's site, as well as Truists response. I am hoping that, once again, the CFPBs intervention convince Truist to read the documents submitted and accept them as sufficient to show insurance coverage, as they have in the past, albeit after months of wrangling.

I had fallen behind on my mortgage payment due to a decrease in my monthly income. In order to prevent a foreclosure, I initially requested a loan modification with my lender, Carrington. However, due to the pandemic the loan fell back into default. Therefore, I decided to sell my property. I hired a real estate company and gave them 3rd party authorization to my mortgage account. They submitted an application for a short sale on my behalf in XXXX XXXX XXXX. Carrington contacted my representative indicating the offer for short sale had been denied, because websites like XXXX and XXXX indicated my home was worth nearly double the purchase contract offer. They also said my home was a 3-family. My real estate representative explained that my home was a 2-family. I provided the Certificate of Occupancy registered with the city. Carrington was also told that comparing my 2-family home with online resources of 3-family homes is inflating the value of my home. Additionally, it is not a legitimate way to evaluate the current condition of my home, which requires a physical inspection by an independent licensed professional. Afterwards, my real estate representative was contacted by individuals that purported themselves to be associated with Carrington and were asking questions regarding my loss mitigation application. They claimed to be from a company named XXXX XXXX. My real estate representative was concerned since this company was unknown to me as an entity associated with my mortgage loan. I thought they might have been fraudsters trying to gain access to my account information. However, Carrington stated XXXX XXXX is an authorized vendor and they had released my loss mitigation information to them without my knowledge. Carrington also stated, XXXX XXXX had the right to approve or deny any Short Sale offer and would make all final decisions. This was a surprise since I do not have a loan with them, had not authorized the release of my personal information to XXXX XXXX and was unclear regarding their role and why I would need their permission to evaluate my loss mitigation options. As time persisted XXXX XXXX only presented the option for a Deed in Lieu. They indicated a Deed in Lieu would give me compensation for relocating. Although I had never requested compensation for relocation, they used this offer to continually coerce me to accept a Deed in Lieu as my only choice for loss mitigation with Carrington. I rejected the Deed in Lieu option and asked to continue to be considered for all loss mitigation options, which XXXX XXXX refused to do. Additionally, XXXX XXXX asked to be allowed to come inside my property. I agreed as long as an independent non-affiliated professional came to evaluate my home. They refused to send a person other than someone from their own company to evaluate the value of my property. After some research, I discovered XXXX XXXX is actually a real estate company that employs agents who work for XXXX XXXX XXXX. I believe XXXX XXXX was acting on their own behalf to try and obtain my property so they could eventually sell it themselves. They had no desire to resolve my foreclosure or engage in my loss mitigation options. This creates a major conflict of interest since they are claiming to evaluate my personal loss mitigation options. XXXX XXXX intentions are disingenuous to me as a homeowner. They stopped evaluating me for all loss mitigation options. They tried to gain access to my property under ill means when their goal is merely self-serving as opposed to resolving my foreclosure in an amicable and fair manner.

During that call, XXXX refused to issue a new check and refused to send me a direct deposit of the escrow refund. XXXX initially refused to connect me with a manager. As was the case the last time, XXXX seemed to be following an informal policy of refusing to connect customers to people with decision-making power. Therefore, I waited for over XXXX minutes to speak with a supervisor, XXXX. I was connected with him at about XXXX minutes. I asked XXXX to have the money routed electronically to a joint bank account that I share with my deceased husband, and he refused on XXXX 's behalf. Initially, he said that under the law, he was not authorized to send payment in any form but check, but I told him that was untrue because other banks are in the XXXX century and deal in electronic refunds and also that I knew that XXXX had a policy of sending electronic transfers when a mistake has been made. I told him that it could easily be classified as a mistake to send the sole owner of a home a check in the name of XXXX people, but still XXXX refused to initiate an electronic transfer of funds. XXXX asked me to hold, but at XXXX minutes, I was provided with the customer service survey and disconnected ( against my will ). To add insult to injury, this is literally the second time in 6 months that this has happened. I made a complaint to the CFPB ( No. XXXX ) against this same mortgage company for the same behavior after receiving a similarly endorsed check. That complaint is obviously documented among the same XXXX parties here and resulted in XXXX finally doing exactly what I had asked for initially : crediting the escrow check to my loan. In the resolution letter, XXXX stated, " At XXXX, we strive to exceed our customers expectations with every interaction. XXXX fell short of this goal and sincerely apologizes for the delay and the resulting confusion. '' The fact that I have to file another complaint shows how shallow and meaningless XXXX 's apology was. In addition to gross insensitivity toward grieving people, what it looks like to me is that XXXX 's internal policies regarding escrow refunds are designed to wrongly enhance its bottom line at the expense of the recently bereaved. That is, if a widow or widower is to ignore XXXX 's malfeasance and not deposit the check, where does that money go before eventually being categorized as " unclaimed ''? Where does the interest that XXXX made on it go? Which executive is paid off the backs of the bereaved? This, when combined with XXXX 's obvious policy of discouraging customers from speaking directly to the management team, is something that is worth the CFPB 's continued attention, even after XXXX resolves this complaint.

I am writing in response to your request for information on fees imposed in residential mortgage transactions. With 24 years of experience as a professional certified XXXX XXXX XXXX, I have observed significant industry changes impacting both consumers and XXXX. When I began my career in 2000, XXXX XXXX were received directly from lenders and brokers, with fees paid either by the borrower directly to the XXXX or by the lender/broker after report completion. Challenges in obtaining payment for XXXX were common if a loan did not close, often resulting in financial losses for XXXX. At that time, the typical fee for a full single-family XXXX in my geographic was around XXXX XXXX {$350.00}. The subprime mortgage crisis brought about the Dodd-Frank Act and the establishment of the CFPB which was to protect consumers. While these measures have had positive effects, they have also introduced negative consequences for both consumers and XXXX. Borrowers are now required to cover not only the appraisal cost but also additional fees imposed by lenders for ordering and processing the appraisal, without clear disclosure. Many lenders prohibit appraisers from including invoices or discussing fees with borrowers, leading to misunderstandings and dissatisfaction by the consumer which reflects negatively on the appraiser. For example, a borrower might believe they paid {$800.00} for an appraisal, while the appraiser receives only {$350.00}. The remaining amount is retained by AMCs ( Appraisal Management Companies ) as processing and sometimes there are additional technology fees charged to the appraiser. Attached are redacted examples to illustrate this issue : XXXX. XXXX XXXX XXXX : Pays {$180.00} for a hybrid report plus a {$20.00} technology fee, resulting in a net payment of {$160.00} to the appraiser. The actual borrower fee remains undisclosed. XXXX. XXXX XXXX XXXX : Offers {$330.00} minus a {$12.00} technology fee, netting {$320.00} to the appraiser. The AMC fee is {$240.00}, with the borrower unknowingly most likely paying {$580.00}. XXXX. XXXX XXXX : Offers {$220.00} for an FHA loan appraisal, a fee level unchanged from 2000, failing to meet the " customary and reasonable '' standards required by Dodd-Frank . These examples highlight the disparity between what borrowers pay and what appraisers receive. The current environment incentivizes AMCs to secure appraisals at the lowest possible cost to maximize their portion of the fee. This often results in appraisers being underpaid relative to the professional standards and costs required to maintain licensure, education, and technology in addition to the consumer unknowingly paying a higher fee than what the appraiser receives under the misleading understanding that they are paying that fee for the appraisal. The customary and reasonable fee requirement must reflect actual payments to appraisers rather than the total borrower charge to cover the cost of a vendor for the lender. The current system allows for non-transparent fee structures that disadvantage both consumers and appraisers. I urge the CFPB to address these discrepancies and ensure transparency in fee structures. Implementing fair compensation standards will help sustain the XXXX XXXX and protect consumer interests. Thank you for your attention to this matter.

If a foreclosure was already scheduled, contact would be made to Select Portfolio Servicing, LLCs counsel to postpone or cancel the sale date. This prevents me from making full payment to SPS and obtaining over {$50000.00} in profit, which would be crucial for me to start over again. I believe SPS practices are consistent with DUAL Tracking, The Dodd-Frank Act, specifically Title X ( the Consumer Financial Protection Act of XXXX ), prohibits a practice known as dual tracking. Dual tracking occurs when a mortgage servicer proceeds with both foreclosure and loss mitigation options while a borrowers application for loan modification is still under review1. This protection ensures that struggling homeowners have a fair process to avoid foreclosure and are not surprised by foreclosure proceedings while exploring available options. This practice violates federal law ( 12 C.F.R. j 1024.41 ) ; The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, which was established by the Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act of 2010, issued mortgage servicing rules that, after being codified into federal law, went into effect as of XX/XX/XXXX. On the XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX Initial Disclosure it states : XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX is to be retained as second home. The current XXXX estimate of that home as of XX/XX/year> is {$410000.00} which will net us a loss of approximately {$30000.00} with fees included. However, on the VA Form 26-1802a HUD V.A. Addendum the same dwelling is stated as to be sold and has a sales price of {$520000.00}. On the initial disclosure forms they stated that we would be bringing {$75000.00} to closing because of sale of real-estate. The lender told me they were just initial documents, and any error would be corrected before closing. In the Department of Veteran Affairs lender handbook Chapter 12 topic 15 and 16 is specifically identifies that the personal well be tested for human consumption and that an uninterested 3rd party must collect and transport the specimen to the testing authority. Further, during the Radon test timeframe, the VA loan appraiser conducted their inspection of the property. As a result, it is difficult to extrapolate real numbers from that test due to the appraiser having to move around the home/basement, open doors, and verify certain minimum property requirements. In theory, that test could have come in much higher. Although it did fail, it does cast doubt on the accuracy of this test. I again emailed our lender and stated that because of this non-compliance, we request that they deny the loan. text: On XX/XX/XXXX, I applied for a Home Equity Line of Credit ( HELOC ) from Better Mortgage through their online portal on the company 's website. I was presented on screen the option to choose between the HELOC and Home Equity Loan. Both options were presented in a side-by-side comparison to show the items like loan amount, payment terms, etc. I chose the HELOC option and then I was instructed to go to the next steps to allow for a " hard credit ''. The hard credit check was confirmed and I received notifications from XXXX and XXXX that my credit had been pulled from Better Mortgage. I was notified on screen ( via pop-up window ) from Better Mortgage 's online portal that I was also approved to expedite my underwriting approval process by submitting all required documentation ( i.e. paystubs, W-2s, tax returns, and other documents ) within the next XXXX window and I can lock in the rate that was provided to me in my side-by-side comparison. Also, this expedited process would mean that I would receive a final approval within XXXX hours after submitting all the required documentation. So, I decided to enter the next phase by submitting all required documentation and it was done all through the company 's online portal driven by a question menu. I answered all questions and submitted documents including my XXXX Bankruptcy dismissal order and I also provided an explanation as to the circumstances surrounding the bankruptcy. I provided a written explanation that said that I had filed bankruptcy XXXX XXXX in XX/XX/XXXX due to under and unemployment at that time but subsequently found a job and then requested the court to withdraw/dismiss the case. The court granted the dismissal and I also provided the official dismissal order as requested by the menu of questions in Better Mortgage 's online portal. Also, I noticed several documents requests ( i.e. relating to income such as W-2s, paystubs, tax returns ) all disappeared from the question menu and noted as " completed. '' I tried calling the phone number provided and subsequently received a denial letter ( Adverse Action Letter ) stating that I needed to have my bankruptcy increase the time since bankruptcy from 0 to 24 months. I called the number again and someone picked the phone and initially stated that my bankruptcy needed to be at least 4 years or more old and when I indicated that it is XXXX XXXX XXXX from filing and XXXX years from dismissal and I explained that I never completed the bankruptcy but rather voluntarily had it dismissed instead, the Better Mortgage rep said that he had to check with his supervisor to double check how many years does the bankruptcy need to be aged on your credit report. He said that he was sorry and that there decision was a hard no given the information even after I explained that I had voluntarily requested to have my bankruptcy case dismissed and provided proof of the dismissal order. He said that there was nothing that he could do at this point. So, I feel that the 100 % online process is deceiving because I find it difficult to believe that their digital process was not able to calculate or detect the age of my bankruptcy when I provided all the details clearly upfront before the " hard credit pull '' as was required by their online portal/digital system.
