I am writing to formally lodge a complaint regarding the practices of all banking and lenders run this same issue however I am specifically talking about my situation with plaza home mortgage. concerning the endorsement of loan documents and the subsequent financial implications that are not disclosed to borrowers. I believe these practices may violate the principles of transparency and fairness as intended by the Truth in Lending Act ( TILA ) and other consumer protection regulations. Lack of Disclosure on Endorsements It has come to my attention that when signing loan documents, borrowers, including myself, are not informed about the different types of indorsements and their potential uses by the lender. Specifically, the use of blank endorsements on these documents allows the lender to transform them into negotiable instruments. These negotiable instruments can then be utilized to secure funds from the Federal Reserve or other financial entities, often with collateral requirements as low as 10 %. Financial Implications and Transparency This practice effectively enables lenders to obtain substantial funds from these endorsed documents without the borrower 's knowledge or consent. The funds obtained through these negotiable instruments are not applied towards reducing the borrowers loan or purchase amount. Instead, they are retained by the lender, often classified as a " gift '' on the books, thereby increasing the lenders financial gain at the expense of the borrower. Regulatory and Legal Considerations Under the Truth in Lending Act ( TILA ), lenders are mandated to provide clear and comprehensive disclosures about the cost of credit, including the annual percentage rate ( APR ), finance charges, amount financed, and the total amount of payments. While TILA does not specifically address the issue of document endorsements, the broader principle of transparency and fairness should encompass the full range of financial implications related to the loan. Case law, such as Rodash v. XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX XXXX ( XXXX Cir. XXXX ), underscores the necessity of full disclosure under TILA. In this case, the court emphasized the importance of clear and complete disclosures to prevent unfair practices. Similarly, in In re Bassett, 285 F.3d 882 ( 9th Cir. 2002 ), the court ruled in favor of the borrower due to the lenders failure to provide adequate disclosures, reinforcing the necessity for lenders to fully inform borrowers of all terms and conditions. Request for Resolution Given the concerns outlined above, I respectfully request the following actions : Full Disclosure : That plaza home mortgage and whomever else provides full and clear disclosure to borrowers regarding the types of endorsements on loan documents and their potential financial implications. Review and Adjustment : That any funds obtained through the use of negotiable instruments derived from my loan documents be reviewed and I have already paid this loan off in full but i fee I am entitled to any funds and interest obtained or gained by my blank endorsement as I was not properly informed of all options or that they would use my document to obtain any additional funds at my expense. Policy Changes : That plaza home mortgage implement policy changes to ensure future borrowers are fully informed about the endorsement process and its potential impact on their loan obligations. I believe these steps are necessary to align with the spirit of XXXX and to uphold the principles of fairness and transparency in lending practices. I look forward to your prompt response and resolution of this matter. Sincerely, XXXX XXXX References to Consider : XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, 16 F.3d 1142 ( 11th Cir. 1994 ) : Case emphasizing the necessity of full disclosure under XXXX. In re XXXX, 285 F.3d 882 ( 9th Cir. 2002 ) : Case highlighting the importance of adequate disclosures to prevent unfair practices.

Strong Protections for Struggling Borrowers The CFPBs mortgage servicing rules ensure that borrowers in trouble get a fair process to avoid foreclosure. Borrowers shouldnt have to worry about mortgage servicers cutting corners or losing applications for relief. They should be told about their options and given time to apply and be considered for loan modifications and other alternatives. Most of all, they shouldnt be surprised by the start of a foreclosure proceeding until they have had time to explore all available options. If they act diligently to seek alternatives, they should not face a foreclosure sale before their applications have been evaluated. The new protections for struggling borrowers include : Restricted Dual-Tracking : Under the CFPBs new rules, dual-tracking when the servicer moves forward with foreclosure while simultaneously working with the borrower to avoid foreclosure is restricted. Servicers can not start a foreclosure proceeding if a borrower has already submitted a complete application for a loan modification or other alternative to foreclosure, and that application is still pending review. To give borrowers reasonable time to submit such applications, servicers can not make the first notice or filing required for the foreclosure process until a mortgage loan account is more than 120 days delinquent.

Here is a recap of my nightmarish experience with ServiceMac LLC ( SM ) during the pandemic : SM advised me that there was no cost to enter into the forbearance arrangement and that they were here to help. In fact, almost all of your correspondence says that but I soon found out that this was just feel-good language that you use but it had nothing to do with reality as your customers could not reach you ; if I did get thru I was told that it would be XXXX days before I could receive a callback. SM encouraged its customers/me to send partial payments whenever I was able. I did so for some months because I wanted to show a good faith effort on my part and also to minimize my financial burden after the forbearance period. Unfortunately for me, all SM did was XXXX up my $ XXXX partial payments ( half of my normal monthly mortgage payment ) with what appears to be largely made-up fees. At XXXX point, SM wrote to me saying that I had an escrow shortage due to an increase in my hazard/homeowners insurance. I asked by phone and by email for SM to apply the recent partial payment to the shortage. I always pay escrow shortages upfront, I did this XXXX with XXXX XXXX then XXXX XXXX. I prefer not to roll over escrow shortages into my loan to avoid interest charged on it for years to come. Your company just ignored my pleas. Finally after weeks of asking, XXXX of your reps said that it could not be done while I was in a forbearance. I kept appealing but to this day I do not know if the shortage was rolled into my loan or not. SM assigned to me more than a half a dozen SPOCs ( single point of contact ) during the forbearance period, a paradox in itself, none of whom I ever spoke with except XXXX. Frustrating is the nicest way that I can describe the lack of continuity and lack of follow-up or follow-through from SM. For weeks at a time, both your Customer Service and Loss Mitigation departments were completely inaccessible to me- the CUSTOMER. When I finally did get a call back or pressed until I got a warm body, your reps did NOT provide any tangible help, just more rhetoric. It became apparent that your Customer Service staff was painfully ill-equipped to handle the needs of your customers during the pandemic. Extremely dissatisfied with SMs lack of responses or answers, I contacted XXXX directly for guidance since this was/is a XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX. A Finance & Loan Analyst there explained XXXX possible approaches that mortgage companies were given to utilize as forbearance exit strategies for their customers. I wrote down each approach with the details as he broke them down for me, answering my questions as I asked him. Yet, when I contacted SM to review these approaches, your company told me that a team of experts reviewed my situation and came up with the best and ONLY exit strategy for me. Best for who? At that point I told your rep that I had XXXX years as a personal finance consultant and teaching debtor education programs. I assured SM I was more than competent to be a part of that conversation and decision. The only response I got to my assertion was that if I did not sign the proposed loan modification, I could face negative consequences going forward since I could not make the lump sum payment to bring my account current. SM would not offer me an option to extend the forbearance another XXXX months once they drafted the modification. Still desperate, I asked SM reps if they knew of any government programs offering help to people like me. I was hearing on the news that such programs were being implemented. SM said No but I believe you all were not forthcoming about this. This is your industry, your line of work and you dont know anything! All you wanted was the hefty profit afforded you through the greedy loan modification you devised and pressured me to sign. I wanted the financial assistance that was available to me because the funds would have brought my account completely current allowing me to get back on track, just as these programs did for so many others. Asking for assistance was rare for me. I am not the type of person who looks for hand-outs, Ive been working since I was XXXX ; I am now XXXX years of age. In the end, SM did NOT abide by any of the guidelines set forth by XXXX. I advised your organization that I was NOT comfortable signing the loan modification agreement without speaking with your so-called experts who devised it- to get my questions answered and my concerns addressed. I knew right off the bat that this agreement was exploitative. Somehow over the next few weeks, SM could contact me more to convince me to sign this unfair loan modification. Your organization practically coerced me into signing it, knowing I did not have many options and hinting at foreclosure as a possible consequence. Unfortunately for me, I did not learn about the specifics of the federal assistance programs and the Louisiana XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXX until after I signed it. This meant I no longer qualified since my mortgage account was technically no longer past due. Had I not been so overwhelmed with taking care of my senior mom at the time who was coming to the end stage of life, Im sure I would have fought this longer. I feel like I deprived my mother of some medical supplies and equipment she desperately needed, wanting to do the right thing by making partial monthly payments to SM. A decision I greatly regret in my grief. For SM to state that the capitalization amount in the loan modification was {$10000.00} provided good optics but the truth is the original loan maturity date on my fixed rate mortgage was XX/XX/year>. So for a forbearance period of a little more than a year, your modification extended my maturity date to XXXX of XXXX adding XXXX months to the life of my loan and thereby increasing my mortgage debt by roughly {$52000.00}! In retrospect, it appears SM was playing a game of evasion with your customers while your Loss Mitigation team cooked up ways to considerably profit off of us who were in the middle of a crisis. Wouldnt it have been more ethical to first recoup the interest that was halted during forbearance, then tack on the months the mortgage was not paid during forbearance and charge reasonable fees for doing so? Not surprising, right after your big windfall, SM simply transferred/sold my mortgage to XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX. The idea that mortgage lenders need liquidity to continue to lend is understandable. But the idea that mortgage servicers can easily and continually profit by packaging and selling loans, means there is absolutely no loyalty to your customers- the mortgagors, because we are a temporary to you ; no reason to provide a good customer experience because we are temporary to you. This short term arrangement almost assures that we as debtors have no means to hold ServiceMac and other mortgage companies accountable for rotten service and unscrupulous activities. However, I am making sure that the Consumer Protection Financial Bureau is watching you. Your company is a debt collector not a service provider and it is wrong for you to tout the untruthful message that you care and you're here to help as we are merely transient debtors to you. So spare me! The pandemic created unprecedented times for both companies and citizens and I took that into consideration with SM but concluded after several months of XXXX ; the name ServiceMac is seriously misleading and I will only agree that SM is a subservicing business if sub stands for below par. Please note that if you have completed a refinance of your original loan the XXXX year requirement resets to the XXXX payment date of your refinanced loan. Please note that all appraisals must be ordered through our offices and are at the expense of the property owner. Per your loans investor requirements, appraisals for PMI removal purposes must be ordered through an unbiased third-party appraisal company approved by the servicer. In order to make certain that we are in compliance with investor requirements, only appraisals ordered through our offices will be acceptable for PMI removal purposes. Please do not send us an appraisal report that was ordered outside of our offices as we will not be able to accept it for PMI removal purposes. We can not take into account local market trends, tax assessments or home value websites as evidence to order an appraisal or to change the LTV. If you have completed substantial STRUCTURAL improvements ( i.e. an addition put on the property or other combined substantial improvements ), please send specifics including what improvements were made, materials used and costs excluding labor. We are requesting this information so we can determine if you are eligible to receive the pre-2 year appraisal information. Loans that are granted the early appraisal, due to approved substantial STRUCTURAL improvements, will only require an 80.00 % LTV for PMI removal eligibility. Loans that are between 2-5 years will need to show a LTV of 75.00 % or 25.00 % equity from an appraisal. If the improvements do not meet the requirements, then you must wait two years to have an appraisal done. With any appraisal, it is possible that the value of the property in question may show an increase in value, but also may in fact show a decrease in value. What are substantial structural improvements? A substantial structural improvement is typically renovations that substantially improve marketability and substantially extend the useful life of the property. This can be a replacement of a major component ( i.e. kitchen renovations replacing cabinet and countertops or bathroom renovation replacing bathroom tile or bathtub ) or significant structural alteration to the property ( i.e. relocating walls, adding additional living space, finishing a basement, garage, deck, or in-ground pool. What are not structural improvements? Cosmetic improvements are not considered structural improvements and will not affect the property value as much as structural improvements. Repairs that are made to keep the property maintained and fully functional are not considered improvements. Cosmetic improvements include : new paint, new siding, a new roof, new carpeting, new flooring, landscaping, new windows, new light fixtures, new appliances or a new heating/air conditioning unit. If you believe that you may be eligible for a pre-2-year appraisal, please email or mail details of the improvements preformed ( in the below/attached format ) and if possible include proof of the cost of improvements ( i.e. receipts or work orders ) in order for us to determine your eligibility. text: My mortgage loan was transferred effective XX/XX/XXXX, which was about halfway between the XX/XX/XXXX official due date and the end of the grace period- XXXX XXXX on which I was planning to make my payment with the original servicer, Guaranteed Rate. I called Shellpoint- the new servicer- shortly after I got the letter advising of the transfer, and informed them of the uncertainty regarding the status of the autopay. The agent I spoke to told me it is totally fine to wait and see if that pulls, since I have a 60-day grace period to make my payments. I was surprised by this generous time frame, and it occurred to me that if I really had a 60 day grace period, I might be able to earn some interest on the funds by waiting until nearly the 60th day to make both the XXXX and XXXX payments. I asked the agent to confirm whether the grace period would allow me to do so without an issue. She balked a bit, and clearly had never been asked that question before. She asked me to wait on a brief hold while she confirmed that with her supervisor. She eventually came back and said that, yes, I could wait until XXXX at the end of the grace period to make my XXXX and XXXX payments ( assuming they didn't get processed by the Guaranteed Rate autopay ), and that would be fine. I thanked her for her help. Finding the long grace period to be perhaps almost too good to be true, I looked up the Federal regulations regarding mortgage servicing transfers, and found that they only protect mortgagees from certain consequences in the event payments are made on time to the original servicer, and arrive late via forwarding to the new servicer. I received a call from another agent on XX/XX/XXXX looking to secure a payment on the account. I relayed to him what I'd been told by the first agent about 6 weeks earlier, but told him that I had been meaning to call anyway out of an abundance of caution. I told him that I had been told there was a grace period running until on or about XX/XX/XXXX, and that because I was told it would not cause me any fees, penalties, or negative credit reporting if I held onto the funds until the 60 days had run, I was planning to pay on or around XX/XX/XXXX. But I added that I'd looked into the regulations which don't require such generous treatment, and that while I had him on the phone, I'd like to confirm that Shellpoint 's policy allows for a grace period of 60 days as I'd been advised. He told me that it's not technically a grace period, and that the other agent should not have used those words. I then said ( at least almost verbatim ) " okay, but just to be clear, my understanding from her is that there would be no negative consequences to my paying my XXXX and XXXX payments, so long as it was done fewer than 60 days after the transfer date. Can you confirm that? '' He then confirmed that there would be no consequences, and asked if I'd like to set up a payment for XXXX, which I did ( though I later cancelled and set up the payment from a different account ). I then began receiving mailings about my " defaulted mortgage, '' but knew based on these two conversations that I didn't need to worry about it. But then I got a {$19.00} fee for property inspection.
